news.headline: City Council Approves Pilot Program to Curb Waze Traffic on Side Streets
news.factual_summary: On April 30, 2019, the Los Angeles City Council voted 12–0 to create a pilot that would seek restrictions on navigation-app routing onto selected streets as a condition of data-sharing agreements. Councilmember Paul Krekorian advocated talks with app developers to address neighborhood traffic and safety concerns. The article notes that the city’s earlier Waze agreement ran from 2015 to 2017. Waze said it was willing to discuss cooperation.

news.headline: New Jersey Town Closes Some City Streets to Drivers Who Don’t Live There
news.factual_summary: Leonia, New Jersey, began barring out-of-town drivers from 60 streets during morning and evening rush hours on the Monday described in the article, with a threatened $200 fine. Officials blamed navigation-app shortcuts toward the George Washington Bridge for congestion and emergency-access problems. Residents were to display yellow vehicle tags, and Waze said it would mark the streets as restricted. Officials defended the restrictions while critics questioned their legality.

news.headline: Delridge Neighborhood Greenway | 26th Ave SW Proposed Diverters: Outreach Summary
news.factual_summary: Seattle’s transportation department paused planned traffic diverters at 26th Avenue SW and SW Brandon and SW Genesee streets after residents raised access concerns. Its November 2020 outreach report compares the original diverters, modified diverters and a local-traffic-only Stay Healthy Street. An online survey received 293 responses, with most respondents dissatisfied with each concept; the Stay Healthy Street drew the most support among the alternatives. The department planned to use the feedback in deciding the next safety treatment.

news.headline: Waze Connected Citizens Program
news.factual_summary: In a December 8, 2014 Waze community post, MGODLEW described the Connected Citizens Program as an exchange of incident and road-closure information between Waze and government partners. The post listed ten initial partners, including Boston, Florida, Utah, Los Angeles County and the New York Police Department, and encouraged members to approach local agencies about joining. The post said sharing data could improve traffic information and incident response.

news.headline: Communication from Public: Council File No. 11-2130-S4
news.factual_summary: The Silver Lake Neighborhood Council voted 18–0 on June 18, 2019 to support retaining Rowena Avenue’s road configuration and adding pedestrian, bicycle and lighting improvements. Its community impact statement also supported a westbound one-way section of Angus Street between Moreno Drive and Kenilworth Avenue, sidewalk feasibility work and further study near Waverly Drive and Glendale Boulevard. The council submitted its statement to the Los Angeles City Clerk on June 24.

news.headline: AB 2015: Department of Transportation: third-party navigation applications: study and report.
news.factual_summary: California’s AB 2015 page records the bill as chaptered on September 14, 2026. Its summary requires Caltrans, in consultation with state, regional and local authorities, to conduct a pilot study of third-party navigation apps’ effects on highways and local roads, including congestion displacement, infrastructure, safety and emergency response. A study and policy recommendations are due by January 1, 2029, with repeal scheduled for January 1, 2033.

news.headline: New ‘absurd’ Dem-backed bill could make your commute longer, California Rep says
news.factual_summary: California Assemblymember Carl DeMaio criticized AB 2015 in a social-media video, warning that studying navigation apps could eventually lead to government-directed routes and longer commutes. Nina Joudeh’s June 16, 2026 report explains that the proposal then imposed no immediate restrictions on navigation platforms. It called for Caltrans and other authorities to study app effects and report recommendations by January 1, 2028. DeMaio warned that government-directed routes could add 30 minutes to commutes.

news.headline: Transportation Motion: Council File 14-1741-S1
news.factual_summary: A Los Angeles transportation motion sought a report from the Department of Transportation on the city’s announced data-sharing partnership with Waze. It asked whether expanding that partnership could reduce cut-through vehicle traffic diverted onto residential streets. The motion contrasted high-capacity roads with smaller streets lacking comparable pedestrian protections and suggested that the city might use its partnership to influence routing.

news.headline: Waze Directions May Skip Certain Streets Under a New City Council Plan
news.factual_summary: Los Angeles’s City Council directed its transportation department to pursue a pilot involving data sharing with navigation-app makers and restrictions on routing along selected streets. Brittany Martin’s May 7, 2019 article describes residents’ complaints about cut-through traffic, emergency access and neighborhood disruption. It also raises unresolved questions about which streets would absorb displaced traffic and whether app makers would cooperate.

news.headline: Waze Hijacked L.A. in the Name of Convenience. Can Anyone Put the Genie Back in the Bottle?
news.factual_summary: Jonathan Littman’s August 2019 feature describes Los Angeles residents’ complaints that navigation apps increased traffic on narrow residential streets. It examines volunteer map editing, residents’ attempts to change routes and researchers’ concerns about individually optimized routing. The city had let its earlier Waze agreement expire and was pursuing a new pilot under Councilmember Paul Krekorian, with LADOT seeking cooperation from app companies. Waze said it was committed to working with cities.

news.headline: Waze restricted due to buildup of side street traffic in Los Angeles
news.factual_summary: On April 30, 2019, the Los Angeles City Council voted 12–0 to approve a pilot intended to restrict navigation-app routing onto certain streets through conditions in data-sharing agreements. Councilmember Paul Krekorian said the city would start discussions with technology companies about reducing neighborhood impacts and improving traffic safety. The report notes that Los Angeles’s previous agreement with Waze ran from 2015 through 2017.

news.headline: ‘Absolute chaos’: Navigation apps blamed for traffic nightmare on one of L.A.’s steepest streets
news.factual_summary: Residents of Baxter Street in Los Angeles’s Echo Park neighborhood told KTLA that navigation-app shortcuts were bringing unfamiliar drivers onto its steep roadway, where they reported crashes and spinouts. Residents supplied photographs and video of incidents and said they had asked Waze to stop treating the street as a shortcut. A meeting with Councilmember Mitch O’Farrell and transportation officials was planned, with a one-way conversion among the options discussed.

news.headline: Walsh announces partnership with traffic app, Waze
news.factual_summary: Boston Mayor Martin Walsh announced a data-sharing partnership with Waze under its Connected Citizens program. City officials said they would send expected road closures to app users and use incoming traffic reports in the Traffic Management Center, where engineers could adjust signals at 550 intersections. The February 19, 2015 report quotes supporters expecting better traffic information and incident responses, while Tufts professor Julian Agyeman argued for reducing traffic rather than only managing it.

news.headline: Boston partners with Waze to clear up clogged streets
news.factual_summary: Boston announced a data-sharing arrangement under which it would provide Waze with information about expected road closures. Waze would send data from roughly 400,000 area drivers to the city’s Traffic Management Center so engineers could use it when adjusting intersection signals. Richard Lawler’s February 21, 2015 report places the agreement within Waze’s Connected Citizens program, which had named Boston among its initial participants the previous year.

news.headline: Using Waze Data to Measure Traffic Congestion
news.factual_summary: Boston’s Analytics Team used aggregated Waze travel data to compare traffic before, during and after the fall 2023 Centre Street safety redesign in West Roxbury. The city reports that illegal speeding fell by more than 75%, while travel times rose by about one minute during daytime and less than two minutes at peak hours. It also reports that Centre Street remained the fastest route 96% of the time despite a slight increase in rerouting. The city planned continued monitoring and nearby speed humps.

news.headline: Waze’s data-sharing program expands across state
news.factual_summary: Massachusetts’s transportation department announced a data-sharing partnership with Waze on the Thursday described in this June 2016 report. Waze would provide anonymous information about traffic bottlenecks, while the state would supply construction, crash and delay information. MassDOT said it planned to use the data in future construction planning. The article notes that Boston had already joined the program and was using Waze data for traffic management.

news.headline: Parts Of Wood Street In West Town To Become One-Way — 3+ Years After Bike Lanes Pitched, Ditched
news.factual_summary: Chicago planned to convert two Wood Street sections to southbound one-way traffic after completing corridor improvements: Cortez to Augusta and Crystal to Division. The June 6, 2025 report says protected-bike-lane and subsequent diverter proposals had been dropped. Work between Division and Ellen was already complete, while further resurfacing, curb improvements and contraflow bike lanes were expected over the following two months. Alderman Daniel La Spata said the changes aimed to discourage cut-through driving while retaining two-way bicycle access.

news.headline: Proposed Switch To One-Way Street On Chicago's Near Northwest Side Is 'Going To Affect Businesses', According To Business Owner
news.factual_summary: A proposal to make Wood Street northbound-only between Ellen Street and Grand Avenue in Chicago drew objections from some residents and businesses in January 2022. The plan paired the conversion with a protected two-way bike lane and had received 67 votes through a ward budgeting process. Business owner Ben Clauss warned of access problems, while Alderman Daniel La Spata said he intended to advance the residents’ selected project. The transportation department would review the proposal after its submission.

news.headline: Shannon Braddock Appointed Acting County Executive; Saka Says He Opposed Traffic Diverters In His Neighborhood Because of Equity Concerns
news.factual_summary: King County’s council unanimously appointed Shannon Braddock acting county executive after Dow Constantine moved to Sound Transit, while a longer appointment through November remained unresolved. In a separate item, PubliCola reported Seattle Councilmember Rob Saka’s comments on traffic cameras and his earlier opposition to proposed diverters at 26th Avenue SW and SW Brandon and SW Genesee streets. Saka cited food-access and equity concerns. The proposed diverters had been canceled following objections.

news.headline: Upcoming opportunities to share feedback on the proposed diverters
news.factual_summary: A September 18, 2020 petition update shared an invitation for Delridge residents to comment on proposed diverters at 26th Avenue SW and SW Brandon and SW Genesee streets. It said installation had stopped in July after community objections and announced a September 30 virtual meeting and an upcoming survey. The notice explained that the greenway was intended to accommodate cycling alongside the RapidRide H Line project. Residents’ feedback would inform the choice of safety treatment.

news.headline: Home Zone: Lake City
news.factual_summary: Seattle’s Lake City Home Zone page described a test of temporary diverters at NE 123rd Street and 28th Avenue NE and at NE 123rd Street and Hiram Place NE. The archived plan scheduled barriers for early spring 2026, traffic monitoring and community feedback later that spring, and a decision on permanent diverters for 2027. Other traffic-calming measures were planned regardless of that decision.

news.headline: Waze’s Maps Now Change as Roads Close
news.factual_summary: Waze added a way for drivers to report complete road closures and explain the disruption. Its system would weigh multiple reports and users’ histories before marking a road closed, redirect other drivers around it, and reopen the route when traffic resumed. The February 2013 article connects the feature to Waze’s Hurricane Sandy work with FEMA and Google Crisis Maps on fuel shortages. Waze also reported a Georgia transportation-department partnership and discussions with other agencies.

news.headline: Navigation App Waze Adds Road Closure Reporting, Says It Now Has 40M Users
news.factual_summary: Waze introduced road-closure reporting on February 27, 2013. Drivers could mark closures and provide reasons and expected duration; the company said it would require enough credible reports before applying a closure and automatically reopen roads on its map when vehicles began using them again. Waze also reported reaching 40 million registered users, with US users supplying 30 million reports in 2012 and map editors making 500 million edits over the preceding year.

news.headline: Waze Connected Citizens Program Factsheet
news.factual_summary: Waze’s Connected Citizens Program factsheet describes a free exchange of driver-reported incidents and slowdowns for agencies’ construction, crash and closure information. It says the program launched with ten partners in October 2014 and had grown to 450. Examples describe Rio de Janeiro using Waze data to adjust election-day traffic staffing and Boston targeting double parking with a Bike Strike Team. The factsheet reported more than 240 move-alongs and 36 tickets during Boston’s month-long test.

news.headline: Waze for Cities
news.factual_summary: A Wazeopedia page posted on September 9, 2021 describes Waze for Cities as a two-way exchange of incident and road-closure data between Waze and government agencies. It lists initial partners, outlines uses for traffic operations and planning, and explains how agencies can apply to participate. The page says partners should offer additional data and technical capability. The page listed safety and traffic-management goals and included a partner list labeled October 2016.

news.headline: Feature Request: Blacklist Areas / Roads
news.factual_summary: Waze community member SilverFoxTV requested a feature on February 13, 2026 that would let users permanently exclude individual roads or custom geographic areas from future routes. The proposal included marking road segments to avoid, defining polygons or radius-based areas, and maintaining a personal exclusion list. The author argued that this would help users respond to safety concerns, road conditions and personal preferences.

news.headline: Waze for Cities
news.factual_summary: Waze’s program page describes tools through which public agencies, road operators and approved event partners can share closures and incidents with drivers and receive traffic reports and analytics. It lists real-time monitoring, emergency alerts, historical congestion analysis and collaboration with volunteer map editors among the available activities. The page says participation is free and describes a monthly free BigQuery analysis allowance.

news.headline: Borough of Mantoloking Council Meeting Minutes — July 21, 2026
news.factual_summary: At Mantoloking’s July 21, 2026 council caucus, resident John Conti urged action against holiday cut-through traffic on Barnegat Lane. Officials discussed temporary access or turn restrictions, regional coordination and traffic engineering. The borough attorney warned of legal difficulties with residents-only restrictions, and the police chief favored broader analysis and temporary signage. The mayor directed staff to explore a traffic engineer and options, with police measures subject to legal review.

news.headline: City of San Francisco Meeting the Smart City Challenge — Volume 2
news.factual_summary: In a May 13, 2016 commitment letter included in San Francisco’s Smart City Challenge application, Smarking offered up to $820,000 in in-kind support. It proposed using parking data for demand management and eventually sending live and predicted occupancy information to connected vehicles. The letter also described planned distribution of BART parking availability through services including Google Maps and Waze.

news.headline: Community Advisory Committee Meeting Packet — September 3, 2025
news.factual_summary: Materials for SFCTA’s September 3, 2025 Community Advisory Committee meeting sought support for $600,000 in design and outreach funding for existing Slow Streets and release of $190,000 reserved for Sanchez Street construction. The materials describe diverters, turn restrictions, traffic calming and monitoring; Sanchez designs include traffic-calming islands and painted safety zones between 23rd and 30th streets. These are allocation requests and staff recommendations in a meeting packet.

news.headline: Alphabet's Tesla Robotaxi Rival Waymo Announces Partnership With Waze To Help Cities Fix Potholes
news.jurisdiction: Multi-jurisdiction (San Francisco Bay Area, Los Angeles, Phoenix, Austin, Atlanta)
news.factual_summary: Waymo announced a Waze partnership to share pothole detections from its vehicles with public agencies and navigation-app users. The initial pilot covered the Bay Area, Los Angeles, Phoenix, Austin and Atlanta, where Waymo said it had identified more than 500 potholes. Users could verify reports, and San Jose's mayor welcomed the potential to identify road damage faster.

news.headline: Can Waymo and Waze fix cities' potholes?
news.jurisdiction: Multi-jurisdiction (San Francisco Bay Area, Los Angeles, Phoenix, Austin, Atlanta)
news.factual_summary: Waymo and Waze announced a pilot using autonomous-vehicle sensors and physical feedback to locate potholes and share road-condition data with transportation agencies through Waze for Cities. Waze users could view and verify detections. Initial coverage included San Francisco, Los Angeles, Phoenix, Austin and Atlanta; Waymo reported 500 identified potholes and planned expansion, including to colder-weather cities.

news.headline: Esri Helps Bring Up-to-Date Road Closure Information to Google Maps and Waze
news.factual_summary: Esri expanded its Community Maps road-closure sharing to Google Maps and Waze through Waze for Cities. ArcGIS users could register their existing closure layers, extending earlier sharing with Apple Maps and TomTom. Esri said more than 100 communities were contributing closure information; participating users could also access Waze feeds of hazards, crashes and traffic conditions.

news.headline: Esri Partners with Waze Connected Citizens Program to Deliver Unprecedented Open Data-Sharing Options to Governments Partnership Enables More Municipalities around the World to Share and Analyze Waze Traffic Data
news.factual_summary: Esri and Waze announced an integration enabling governments to exchange traffic information through ArcGIS and the Connected Citizens Program. Municipalities could share road closures and receive anonymous incident and slowdown reports for analysis and existing operations systems. The companies said the arrangement could reduce reliance on sensor investment and improve planning.

news.headline: Waze and Waycare strike data-sharing pact to improve city traffic
news.jurisdiction: United States (Southern Nevada / Las Vegas, Tampa, Delaware)
news.factual_summary: Waze and Waycare agreed to share traffic information. Waycare combined sources such as cameras, weather, connected vehicles and public agencies for transport operations; the partnership would add Waze user data and send agency-verified incidents to drivers through the app. CEO Noam Maital said the exchange would connect municipalities and emergency services with travelers. The article also described Waycare projects in Nevada and other states.

news.headline: The U.S. government wants to regulate Google Maps all other car navigation apps
news.factual_summary: The Obama administration’s proposed transportation legislation would give the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration authority over vehicle navigation aids, including smartphone apps such as Google Maps and Waze. Officials said the agency could demand changes to dangerous apps after release rather than approve them beforehand. Technology companies questioned enforceability.

news.headline: Stuck in Traffic? Thanks, Obama!: Feds to Regulate Waze, Google Maps, and Other Navigation Apps
news.jurisdiction: United States (Federal & California state law case study)
news.factual_summary: A Reason commentary opposed proposed transportation-bill provisions extending federal safety oversight to smartphone navigation apps such as Waze and Google Maps. It argued restrictions could hinder useful tools and cited a California appeals court’s reversal of Steven Spriggs’s conviction for consulting a phone map while driving.

news.headline: Alert system to warn Illinois drivers about traffic risks, remind them of Scott's Law
news.factual_summary: Illinois State Police and the state technology department partnered with HAAS Alert to expand move-over warnings to supported vehicle displays. Police send location information about incidents or other hazards to Safety Cloud, which alerts approaching drivers to slow down and change lanes. The initiative builds on existing Waze and Google Maps alerts and is intended to protect roadside troopers and drivers.

news.headline: GREENSBORO CITY ANNOUNCES PARTNERSHIP WITH MOBILE APP WAZE
news.factual_summary: Greensboro announced a Waze Connected Citizens partnership exchanging city closures, construction and event notices for anonymous user incident and slowdown reports. Officials said the arrangement would improve advance traffic information and help drivers choose routes. The release also cited Waze user statistics and a satisfaction ranking.

news.headline: City Announces Partnership with Mobile App Waze
news.factual_summary: Greensboro announced a Waze Connected Citizens partnership exchanging city closures, construction and event notices for anonymous user incident and slowdown reports. Officials said the arrangement would improve advance traffic information and help drivers choose routes. The release also cited Waze user statistics and a satisfaction ranking.

news.headline: Filling in data gaps and potholes: Atlanta one of five cities areas to partner with Waymo and Waze on filling in potholes
news.factual_summary: Waymo and Waze included Atlanta in a five-city pilot mapping potholes with autonomous-vehicle sensors and user data. The companies reported more than 500 detections across the initial cities and hoped to expand to colder regions. The article described Atlanta's existing ATL311 reporting system and Pothole Posse repair crews as the local maintenance context.

news.headline: Waymo , Waze to detect potholes for cities
news.factual_summary: Waymo and Waze announced a five-market pilot sharing vehicle-detected potholes with public agencies and Waze users. The companies reported about 500 detections across the initial areas. San Jose's mayor welcomed the collaboration, while San Francisco officials and former transportation director Jeffrey Tumlin raised questions about repair funding, municipal coordination and coverage of neighborhoods beyond frequently traveled routes.

news.headline: Waymo partners with navigation app to help identify potholes in cities, including Austin - The Daily Texan
news.factual_summary: Waymo and Waze began sharing vehicle-detected pothole information with Austin transportation officials and navigation-app users. An Austin official said staff had received an initial dataset and were validating its accuracy before possible use in pavement-maintenance planning. Waymo described the free data as supplementing existing city tools; residents could continue reporting road issues through Austin 311.

news.headline: DOTD and Baton Rouge City-Parish Announce Partnership with Waze
news.factual_summary: Louisiana DOTD and Baton Rouge City-Parish announced a free Waze partnership exchanging government construction, crash and closure reports for anonymous user incidents and traffic information. Both agencies planned to integrate incoming data into traffic-management tools; Waze information was expected on 511la.org by summer’s end. Officials anticipated better commuting and emergency information.

news.headline: Waze integrates city data-sharing program with Google Cloud
news.factual_summary: Waze made its city data-sharing program available through Google Cloud, adding BigQuery analytics and Data Studio visualizations to help agencies interpret traffic information. Previously, partners had to ingest and store an API feed themselves. The program, renamed Waze for Cities Data, offered standard dashboards and limited free storage and analysis allowances, with paid options for additional use. Public agencies could apply to join.

news.headline: Google told drivers to drive a longer way on purpose
news.factual_summary: Google researchers tested rerouting small shares of Maps drivers in ten U.S. cities over six months to spread congestion. The study reported average speed gains of 2% on congested roads and 0.7% shorter travel times, with some diverted drivers taking longer routes. Researchers discussed modest emissions benefits and induced-demand risks; California legislation seeking study of navigation-app impacts awaited the governor.

news.headline: CITY OF BOSTON PARTNERS WITH GOOGLE ON TRAFFIC SIGNAL OPTIMIZATION
news.factual_summary: Boston announced a Google Project Green Light partnership that uses AI and Maps driving trends to recommend traffic-signal adjustments. City engineers had implemented four recommendations after reviewing safety and feasibility. The city reported over-50% reductions in stop-and-go traffic at two intersections and planned to consider further changes. The system analyzes traffic after implementation to support continued monitoring.

news.headline: Google maps shortcut to turnpike causing headaches on Turner's County Road
news.factual_summary: Turner's Select Board considered weight restrictions and advisory signs to discourage heavy trucks from using County Road as a shortcut to the Maine Turnpike in Auburn. Residents had complained about speeding, trucks and unsafe lane use. Town Manager Kurt Schaub said Google Maps recommended the route and considered contacting Google. The board had made no decision at the reported meeting.

news.headline: San Antonio River Authority partners with Waze app to provide live low-water crossing data
news.factual_summary: The San Antonio River Authority announced a collaboration linking BEXARflood.org with Waze to provide real-time low-water-crossing information. The flood website draws on more than 190 Bexar County sensors and identifies safe roads, rising water and closures. Officials said the integration, already linked for several months, gives drivers additional information during adverse weather and is intended to improve road safety.

news.headline: City announces data-sharing partnership with WAZE aimed at improving traffic in Boston
news.factual_summary: Boston Mayor Martin Walsh announced a Waze data-sharing partnership that would distribute planned road closures and supply aggregated traffic information to the city’s Traffic Management Center. Waze data was already informing signal-timing decisions alongside camera feeds. Officials planned spring congestion-management pilots, including evaluating MBTA signal priority, with before-and-after speed comparisons.

news.headline: Google 's Waze Crowdsourced Traffic and Navigation App is a Hit, But How Does It Impact Privacy, the Law and Google Maps?
news.factual_summary: Research and Markets announced a report examining Waze’s crowdsourced mapping, user engagement, advertising, relationship with Google Maps and implications for privacy and law enforcement. The announcement promoted real-time traffic sharing and other app features and listed the report’s topics.

news.headline: Waymo robotaxis are helping cities map potholes. Could Philly be next? The self-driving car company is partnering with Waze, the crowdsourced GPS navigation app, on a pilot program to map potholes in five cities.
news.factual_summary: Waymo announced a five-market pothole-mapping pilot with Waze and said it would expand the service to Philadelphia alongside future ride-hailing operations. The company was testing there but lacked Pennsylvania approval to carry passengers and had no launch timeline. Sensor detections would be shared with agencies through Waze for Cities and supplement driver-reported potholes.

news.headline: New Milford, Kent to ban commercial buses from driving on South Kent Road
news.factual_summary: New Milford’s council voted June 23 to recommend banning commercial buses from South Kent Road after residents reported safety, congestion and property concerns. Officials planned coordination with Kent and Connecticut DOT on restrictions and signage, while a council member suggested asking Waze to remove the road from suggested routes. Club Getaway’s operator supported restrictions and said the business had encouraged bus companies to avoid the road.

news.headline: NORFOLK JOINS WAZE CONNECTED CITIZENS PROGRAM
news.factual_summary: Norfolk announced a free Waze partnership exchanging city construction, crash and road-closure information for anonymous user incidents and slowdown data. City manager Douglas Smith said the exchange would help residents and staff make travel decisions. The announcement also described advance notices for major events and the partners’ intention to use shared information for traffic planning.

news.headline: Smartphone Navigation And Maps Applications Could Soon Be Regulated By The Transportation Department
news.factual_summary: Android Headlines reported that the Transportation Department was seeking congressional authority to regulate smartphone navigation apps to address driver distraction. Potential restrictions remained unspecified, and the article said changes would concern apps deemed dangerous rather than a complete ban. The writer questioned the need for regulation given voice controls.

news.headline: MAYOR GARCETTI DETAILS AGREEMENT WITH WAZE TO HELP REDUCE CONGESTION, INCREASE SAFETY, AND IMPROVE DRIVING EXPERIENCE AROUND L.A.
news.factual_summary: Los Angeles Mayor Eric Garcetti detailed a data-sharing agreement with Waze: the city would provide closures, construction and hazards, while receiving aggregated traffic and incident reports. He also announced planned hit-and-run notifications and AMBER alerts. The city was exploring integration into its 311 system and future traffic-management evaluation.

news.headline: Commercial buses to be banned from South Kent Road
news.factual_summary: New Milford’s council voted June 23 to recommend banning commercial buses from South Kent Road after residents reported safety, congestion and property concerns. Officials planned coordination with Kent and Connecticut DOT on restrictions and signage, while a council member suggested asking Waze to remove the road from suggested routes. Club Getaway’s operator supported restrictions and said the business had encouraged bus companies to avoid the road.

news.headline: City of Sacramento Joins Waze Connected Citizens Program
news.factual_summary: Sacramento announced a free Waze partnership exchanging government closures, construction and event information for anonymous incident and slowdown data. Officials intended to analyze the feed for event management and congestion strategies, with a full program launch anticipated by fall 2016.

news.headline: Street Smarts: Waymo and Waze Turn Driver Data Into Pothole Repairs
news.factual_summary: Waymo and Waze announced a pilot to share pothole detections from autonomous vehicles with transportation agencies through Waze for Cities and with Waze drivers. Initial markets were Austin, Atlanta, Los Angeles, Phoenix and the San Francisco Bay Area, with expansion planned. The article attributed the project to city officials' requests for better road-condition information.

news.headline: New Waymo , Waze pilot project will help Atlanta officials find potholes
news.factual_summary: Waymo and Waze included Atlanta in a five-market pilot sharing pothole detections with transportation agencies and app users. The companies said vehicle data would supplement existing driver reports and city inspections, with 500 potholes identified across the initial markets. The article placed the project alongside Atlanta's revived Pothole Posse repair program and described plans to expand the data partnership.

news.headline: CITY OF ARLINGTON JOINS WAZE CONNECTED CITIZENS PROGRAM
news.factual_summary: Arlington, Texas, announced a free Waze Connected Citizens partnership, exchanging city construction, crash and closure data for anonymous user incidents and slowdown reports. Officials intended to use the data to understand road conditions and inform operations and planning, including major-event notices.

news.headline: Lower Your Carbon Footprint With Google Maps New Eco Friendly Routing Feature
news.factual_summary: Google launched eco-friendly routing to display fuel-efficient alternatives alongside the fastest Maps route. The article said calculations considered road incline and congestion, drawing on work with the National Renewable Energy Laboratory. Users could compare estimated fuel savings and arrival times. Google also announced bicycle and scooter information updates and projected that efficient routing could reduce annual emissions.

news.headline: Waymo and Waze are teaming up to save your car tires from potholes
news.factual_summary: Waymo and Waze announced a pilot sharing robotaxi pothole detections through Waze for Cities with transportation agencies and app users, who could verify reports. Initial coverage included the San Francisco Bay Area, Los Angeles, Phoenix, Austin and Atlanta. Waymo said it had already identified about 500 potholes across those areas; the data would supplement existing user reports.

news.headline: BUSINESS Waymo, Waze team up to map L.A.'s potholes
news.factual_summary: Waymo and Waze launched a pothole-detection pilot in Los Angeles and four other markets, sharing vehicle data with public agencies and app users. Los Angeles street-services officials were discussing the program with Waymo. The report cited rising 311 pothole complaints after heavy rain and lower recent paving totals; the companies said their data would supplement resident reports and help identify repair needs.

news.headline: How Waymo and Waze are pitching in to help solve L.A.'s pothole problem
news.factual_summary: Waymo and Waze launched a pothole-detection pilot in Los Angeles and four other markets, sharing vehicle data with public agencies and app users. Los Angeles street-services officials were discussing the program with Waymo. The report cited rising 311 pothole complaints after heavy rain and lower recent paving totals; the companies said their data would supplement resident reports and help identify repair needs.

news.headline: NAPERVILLE AND EVANSTON 1ST ILLINOIS PARTNERS TO JOIN WAZE CONNECTED CITIZENS PROGRAM
news.factual_summary: Evanston and Naperville announced Waze Connected Citizens partnerships, exchanging construction, closure and event information for anonymous user incidents and slowdown reports. Officials intended to use the data for traveler awareness and future infrastructure planning.

news.headline: Charlotte works with Waze transportation app
news.factual_summary: Charlotte announced a Waze Connected Citizens partnership to exchange city construction information and driver-reported road data. Officials said the app would help travelers see current conditions and alternative routes while giving the city another source for evaluation.

news.headline: Government seeks to regulate maps apps
news.factual_summary: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration was developing handheld-device distraction guidelines and seeking clarification of its authority through the proposed GROW AMERICA Act. The article says mandatory regulations were not currently planned, distinguishing this work from the agency’s existing voluntary dashboard guidelines. It also reports a national enforcement and advertising campaign encouraging drivers to put devices away.

news.headline: RALEIGH PARTNERS WITH WAZE CONNECTED CITIZENS PROGRAM
news.factual_summary: Raleigh announced its Waze Connected Citizens partnership and said it was sharing special-event and full road-closure information drawn from right-of-way permits. Officials described making existing city data accessible through an app already used by travelers.

news.headline: DEPARTMENT CREATES PARTNERSHIP WITH WAZE
news.factual_summary: Oregon’s Department of Transportation announced a two-way data partnership with Waze. TripCheck construction, incidents, weather and road reports, updated every two minutes, were supplied to the app, while Waze user reports were fed to the department. ODOT was assessing how to filter incoming data and planned to enhance TripCheck later.

news.headline: LOUDOUN COUNTY WORKS WITH WAZE TO IMPROVE TRAFFIC INFORMATION
news.factual_summary: Loudoun County began feeding sheriff’s incident information from its dispatch systems directly to Waze, where reports appeared under LoudounCoSO. The county also received Waze traffic information for mapping and analysis. Officials said the exchange would help travelers choose routes and understand closures. The partnership used the county’s GIS infrastructure and was among the initial applications available through its new GeoHub.

news.headline: MAYOR WALSH ANNOUNCES DATA-SHARING PARTNERSHIP WITH WAZE AIMED AT IMPROVING TRAFFIC IN BOSTON
news.factual_summary: Boston Mayor Martin Walsh announced a Waze data-sharing partnership that would distribute planned road closures and supply aggregated traffic information to the city’s Traffic Management Center. Waze data was already informing signal-timing decisions alongside camera feeds. Officials planned spring congestion-management pilots, including evaluating MBTA signal priority, with before-and-after speed comparisons.

news.headline: VIRGINIA BEACH WINS 2020 GOVERNMENT EXPERIENCE AWARD FOR TRAFFIC DATA-SHARING PARTNERSHIP
news.factual_summary: Virginia Beach received a Center for Digital Government project award for its traffic-data partnership with Waze. The free exchange gave the city anonymous driver reports of incidents and slowdowns, while the city supplied construction, crash and closure information. Officials described using the information for traffic management during events and disasters and sharing it with travelers, emergency responders and regional authorities.

news.headline: VIRGINIA BEACH JOINS WAZE CONNECTED CITIZENS PROGRAM
news.factual_summary: Virginia Beach announced a free data-sharing partnership with Waze, led by its emergency-management office. The city would receive anonymous driver reports of incidents and slowdowns and provide construction, crash and closure data. Officials planned to use the exchange to manage special-event and incident traffic and provide advance warnings about flooding and major events.

news.headline: Why Some Cities Have Had Enough of Waze
news.factual_summary: A reported feature examined conflicts between Waze shortcuts and municipal traffic plans. Los Angeles councilmember David Ryu sought legal review, while residents and officials elsewhere described closures, turn restrictions and attempts to submit false reports. Waze defended routing on public roads and said legal restrictions would be reflected in its maps. Researchers discussed access controls and predictive approaches that account for drivers’ responses to route information.

news.headline: Fort Worth Joins Waze Connected Citizens Program
news.factual_summary: Fort Worth launched a free Waze Connected Citizens partnership to exchange city construction, crash and closure information for anonymous driver incidents and slowdown reports. The city could also provide advance notices of parades and other major events. Officials expected better traffic awareness and planning.

news.headline: Judge nixes New Jersey town's ban on nonresident drivers
news.factual_summary: A New Jersey judge struck down Leonia’s nonresident traffic restrictions because the borough had not obtained required state transport approval for closures affecting a state roadway. Mayor Judah Zeigler said the town would seek a stay, appeal and introduce revised ordinances. The restrictions had responded to navigation-app shortcuts toward the George Washington Bridge; a nearby resident who sued welcomed the ruling.

news.headline: PennDOT launches 'know your height' campaign to combat bridge strikes
news.factual_summary: PennDOT launched a multistate campaign urging drivers to know their vehicle height and check low-clearance routes to prevent bridge strikes. Officials cited more than 600 Pennsylvania strikes from 2013–2023 and recent covered-bridge damage. The campaign targets commercial, delivery, rental-truck and RV drivers, emphasizing posted clearances and PA511 route information rather than relying solely on ordinary navigation apps.

news.headline: ANCHORAGE JOINS WAZE CONNECTED CITIZENS PROGRAM
news.factual_summary: Anchorage announced a free Waze Connected Citizens partnership. The municipality would share construction and road-closure data and receive anonymous user incident and slowdown reports. Chief innovation officer Brendan Babb said the exchange would help travelers during the short construction season and support analysis of road conditions. The announcement also described possible future notices for parades and other major events.

news.headline: Nevada Department of Transportation Announces Traffic-Reporting Partnership with Waze Connected Citizens Program
news.factual_summary: Nevada’s transportation department announced a free Waze data-sharing partnership. NDOT would send construction, incident and closure information to the app and receive anonymous user reports for traffic operations and dispatch. Officials planned to begin internal use in coming months and later display updates through Nevada 511. The announcement also urged motorists to set up trips before driving and use mounted phones and hands-free functions.

news.headline: Navigation Apps Making Secret Shortcuts Very Public in Communities
news.factual_summary: CBS reported Leonia, New Jersey’s plan to restrict rush-hour access to roughly 60 residential streets beginning January 22. Officials blamed navigation-app shortcuts toward the George Washington Bridge for neighborhood congestion and safety concerns. Residents and businesses would receive yellow access tags, while unauthorized drivers faced $200 tickets. Main roads would remain open, and Waze said its maps reflected local restrictions and changing road conditions.

news.headline: CARY MARKS OPEN DATA DAY BY JOINING WAZE CONNECTED CITIZENS PROGRAM
news.factual_summary: Cary announced a Waze partnership exchanging construction, crash and street-closure data for anonymous driver incidents and slowdown reports. A Waze-generated map was available through the town website. Officials planned to expand the outgoing feed from a small group of departments to all departments later in the year.

news.headline: RIDOT RETURNING TRAVEL TIMES TO HIGHWAY MESSAGE BOARDS NEW PARTNERSHIP WITH WAZE SAVES $200,000 ANNUALLY
news.factual_summary: Rhode Island’s transportation department partnered with Waze to restore travel-time displays on highway message boards. The free data replaced information for which RIDOT said it had paid $200,000 annually. Travel times were to appear on four boards starting November 20, with more signs added later. RIDOT would exchange construction, crash and closure reports for anonymous Waze traffic and incident information.

news.headline: DOUGLAS COUNTY JOINS WAZE CONNECTED CITIZENS PROGRAM
news.factual_summary: Douglas County, Colorado, announced a Waze Connected Citizens partnership to exchange government construction and closure information for anonymous driver traffic data. Officials expected the arrangement to improve awareness of roadworks and support commuting decisions.

news.headline: EVANSTON AND NAPERVILLE 1ST ILLINOIS PARTNERS TO JOIN WAZE CONNECTED CITIZENS PROGRAM
news.factual_summary: Evanston and Naperville announced Waze Connected Citizens partnerships, exchanging construction, closure and event information for anonymous user incidents and slowdown reports. Officials intended to use the data for traveler awareness and future infrastructure planning.

news.headline: MIAMI-DADE COUNTY IS 1ST COUNTY IN FLORIDA TO JOIN WAZE CONNECTED CITIZENS PROGRAM
news.factual_summary: Miami-Dade County announced a Waze Connected Citizens partnership to exchange government construction, crash and road-closure data for anonymous user traffic information. Transportation, IT and water departments were participating, with police involvement planned later. Officials hoped real-time information would improve routing and mobility for residents.

news.headline: MASSDOT JOINS WAZE CONNECTED CITIZENS PROGRAM, TWO-WAY DATA SHARE HOPES TO EASE TRAFFIC CONGESTION IN MASSACHUSETTS
news.factual_summary: MassDOT announced a free two-way Waze partnership, exchanging state construction, crash and closure reports for anonymous user incidents and slowdown information. The agency said the partnership would also enable historical-data compilation for future road planning. Officials anticipated better traveler information, safety and investment decisions.

news.headline: Penndot To Partner With Waze
news.factual_summary: Pennsylvania Governor Tom Wolf announced a free two-way partnership between PennDOT and Waze. The agency would provide road-condition reports to the app and receive crowdsourced incidents and slowdown information to supplement internal traffic monitoring. Officials anticipated improved traveler information and quicker awareness of congestion.

news.headline: Mayor Lee Announces Data Sharing Partnership with Waze to Minimize Congestion & Maximize Reliability for Drivers & Transit Riders
news.factual_summary: San Francisco Mayor Ed Lee announced a free Waze partnership to share city closures, construction and event information and receive anonymous traffic and incident data. The city intended to use the feed for event management, parking-control deployment and evaluation of congestion strategies, including around Super Bowl activities.

news.headline: Town that closed streets to commuters gets court reprieve
news.factual_summary: A New Jersey appeals panel sent Leonia’s residential-street restrictions back to the state transportation department for reconsideration. The court found that the department had inadequately investigated before declaring the ordinances invalid. Leonia had restricted commuter cut-through traffic routed toward the George Washington Bridge by navigation apps. The panel required a fuller review of the ordinances and supporting documents under the statutory criteria.

news.headline: Iowa DOT joins Waze Connected Citizens program to give motorists in Iowa access to more real-time traveler information
news.factual_summary: Iowa’s Department of Transportation announced a Waze Connected Citizens partnership and launched a Waze layer in its 511 traveler-information system. The layer displayed filtered user reports of crashes, congestion, closures and hazards, marked as Waze reports. In exchange, Iowa supplied its 511 feed to Waze at no charge.

news.headline: Towns cracking down on GPS app shortcuts
news.factual_summary: A UPI report described communities responding to navigation-app shortcuts with access restrictions, prohibited turns, traffic calming and data-sharing agreements. Examples included Leonia, Medford and Fremont, alongside concerns from Los Angeles and London. Google said its routing reflected lawful road conditions; Waze defended use of public streets and said false incident reports were corrected through other users’ data. Officials discussed safety, enforceability and the risk of shifting traffic elsewhere.

news.headline: CITY OF ASHEVILLE PARTNERS WITH WAZE TRAVEL APP TO ADD OFFICIAL TRAFFIC INFORMATION
news.factual_summary: Asheville announced a Waze partnership and a tailored GIS feed supplying permitted construction, lane closures and street closures in real time. Previously, users had needed to mark closures themselves. The city would also receive anonymous incidents and slowdown reports through Connected Citizens.

news.headline: TRAFFIC APP A TWO-WAY STREET
news.factual_summary: Hillsborough County described its first year exchanging road-closure and shelter information with Waze. Officials said driver feedback helped identify trouble spots, while a commuter described using the app to choose among routes to Tampa. Public Works was evaluating how recurring user reports could supplement other data and trigger studies of signal changes or additional lanes. County and regional agencies participated in the partnership.

news.headline: Samsara Launches Leading Commercial Navigation Solution to Boost Safety and Compliance for U.S. Trucking Fleets Leading commercial GPS navigation solution helps U.S. trucking fleets avoid bridge strikes and other hazards on the road
news.factual_summary: Samsara launched Commercial Navigation in the United States, integrating truck-specific directions into its Driver App. The company said routes account for vehicle height, weight and hazardous-material restrictions and provide railroad-crossing warnings. Features include an hours-of-service display over the map and dispatcher route updates. Samsara and a trucking customer described expected safety, compliance and operational benefits.

news.headline: CORAL GABLES JOINS WAZE CONNECTED CITIZENS PROGRAM
news.factual_summary: Coral Gables announced a free, two-way data-sharing partnership with Waze through its Connected Citizens Program. Waze would provide anonymous driver reports of incidents and slowdowns, while the city would supply construction, crash and closure information and advance notice of major events. City officials planned to use the information to understand traffic conditions and support transportation planning.

news.headline: BLUMENTHAL DEMANDS TECH COMPANIES UPGRADE GPS APPS AFTER TRUCKS HIT OVERPASSES
news.factual_summary: Senator Richard Blumenthal renewed his request that Google and Apple add height, weight and hazardous-material restrictions to Waze, Google Maps and Apple Maps. Citing continued truck bridge strikes, he asked for clear route warnings and suggested a commercial-vehicle user setting. His April 6 release included letters seeking responses by April 19 and described earlier company correspondence stating the apps were designed for passenger vehicles.

news.headline: NYPD Demands Google GPS App Stop Helping People Get Around DUI Checkpoints
news.factual_summary: The NYPD demanded that Google stop Waze users from sharing information that could help drivers avoid sobriety checkpoints. Its February 2 letter argued that checkpoint posts could impede enforcement. A Waze spokesperson said the app marked general police presence rather than offering a dedicated checkpoint alert, and defended the feature as encouraging drivers to obey traffic laws. Users could add checkpoint details in comments.

news.headline: Reps. Latimer, Bresnahan Introduce Legislation to Prevent Bridge Strikes by Large Trucks Rep. George Latimer (D- NY ) News Release
news.factual_summary: Representatives George Latimer and Rob Bresnahan introduced the Bridges Not Bumpers Act of 2025 to address commercial-vehicle strikes on low bridges. The bill would establish a federal working group on clearance data, truck navigation and vehicle labeling, a national strike-data clearinghouse, and research grants for countermeasures. Trucking and railroad trade groups endorsed the proposal.

news.headline: MAYOR WU ANNOUNCES EXPANSION OF PROJECT GREEN LIGHT SIGNAL OPTIMIZATION PROGRAM
news.factual_summary: Boston expanded Google Project Green Light signal optimization to 114 intersections across 20 neighborhoods. The city said engineers assessed AI-generated recommendations and partnered with INRIX to evaluate changes. During the second pilot phase, it reported average delay reductions of 13.5% and 20% fewer unnecessary stops at newly retimed intersections, with larger changes at some locations. Officials planned continued expansion and monitoring.

news.headline: CALTRANS PARTNERS WITH WAZE CONNECTED CITIZENS PROGRAM
news.factual_summary: Caltrans announced a free two-way Waze partnership. Waze would supply anonymous traffic and user incident reports for Caltrans traveler information, while the agency would send construction, closures and road conditions to the app. Officials expected the combined feeds to improve trip planning and road awareness.

news.headline: Navigational apps may create traffic woes; Woodland Heights to slow detouring drivers with speed cushions, traffic circles
news.factual_summary: Houston’s Woodland Heights neighborhood and city engineers planned temporary speed cushions and traffic circles to address speeding and cut-through traffic that residents associated with navigation apps. Earlier petitions and a traffic study led to recommended sites. A 90–210-day evaluation and resident approval would precede permanent changes, with voluntary neighborhood contributions and city funding. An exact installation date had not been announced.

news.headline: Waze, LA Cops Bury The Hatchet, Figure Out A Way To Cooperatively Help People
news.factual_summary: Techdirt welcomed Los Angeles’ announced cooperation with Waze to share hit-and-run and kidnapping alerts after police criticism of the app’s police-location reports. The writer argued that earlier safety objections concealed concern about ticket revenue and portrayed the partnership as a constructive use of crowdsourcing. The alerts were expected to roll out over the coming months.

news.headline: Google Maps now shows speed traps, draws police ire
news.factual_summary: Google began adding reports of speed traps, crashes and slowdowns to Maps on iPhones, alongside new incident categories for both iOS and Android. Police had objected that checkpoint reporting could help impaired drivers evade enforcement. Google defended the safety benefits of alerts, while the NYPD said discussions with the company were productive. Maps offered speed-trap reports; Waze also allowed comments describing police activity.

news.headline: AUSTIN TRANSPORTATION AND WAZE PARTNER TO SHARE REAL-TIME TRAFFIC UPDATES
news.factual_summary: Austin Transportation began exchanging information with Waze. The city supplied scheduled special-event road closures so the app could notify users and reroute trips, while its Transportation Management Center received anonymous reports of major delays for targeted signal adjustments. Director Robert Spillar said the partnership offered a broader view of road conditions than the city could obtain through additional fixed detection equipment alone.

news.headline: ALDOT Joins Waze Connected Citizens Program
news.factual_summary: Alabama’s transportation department announced a free Waze partnership, supplying construction, crash and closure information in exchange for anonymous user traffic reports. Incoming Waze data was to be integrated into ALGOTraffic.com to supplement incident management and traveler information. Officials anticipated improved awareness and mobility.

news.headline: LINCOLN JOINS WAZE CONNECTED CITIZENS PROGRAM
news.factual_summary: Lincoln joined Waze’s Connected Citizens Program to exchange city closures and construction information for anonymous driver reports. A public-works official said the data could support signal-timing work under Green Light Lincoln and inform planning. The city also advised travelers to set destinations before moving, rely on voice guidance and let passengers operate navigation tools where possible.

news.headline: Partnership with traffic app could help ease congestion
news.factual_summary: Johns Creek announced a free Waze partnership exchanging city road-closure, construction and maintenance information for crowdsourced traffic data. Officials said the feed could fill gaps where cameras or sensors were absent and inform signal timing, construction and spending decisions. They hoped drivers would choose better routes.

news.headline: OK Waze, NYPD wants you to stop reporting locations of DUI checkpoints
news.factual_summary: The NYPD asked Google to stop users sharing sobriety-checkpoint locations through Waze and associated platforms, arguing that the reports could help impaired drivers evade enforcement. Waze said its police icon represented general police presence, with checkpoint details possible through comments. The company defended the feature as encouraging careful driving and compliance with traffic laws. The department’s February 2 letter threatened further legal action.

news.headline: VDOT PARTNERS WITH WAZE CONNECTED CITIZENS PROGRAM TO IMPROVE TRAVEL ON VIRGINIA 'S ROADWAYS
news.factual_summary: VDOT and Waze launched a two-way traffic-information partnership. Waze would provide anonymous user incidents and slowdown reports to complement 511Virginia, while VDOT would supply verified construction, crash and closure data. Officials described advance information about planned events and better traveler awareness.

news.headline: Colorado Transportation Officals Asked Navigation App Providers To Plant False Information. Worse, The Providers Complied.
news.factual_summary: Techdirt criticized Colorado officials for asking navigation providers to show Highway 82 and Independence Pass as closed while the road remained open, to discourage diversions during an Interstate 70 closure. Citing records reported by the Aspen Times, it described requests to Google, Waze, Apple and TomTom and conflicting information on CDOT’s own site. The author argued that false closure notices undermined trust.

news.headline: Police want Waze to stop displaying DWI checkpoint locations
news.factual_summary: The NYPD asked Google to stop Waze users sharing police and sobriety-checkpoint locations, arguing that reports could help impaired drivers evade enforcement. Waze said it had no dedicated checkpoint feature and that users supplied those details manually. The author questioned the legal basis of the demand and raised free-speech concerns about restricting crowdsourced information.

news.headline: Lawmakers map future for directional aids; Bills would exempt car navigation systems from bans, despite concerns of consumer groups
news.factual_summary: New York lawmakers were considering bills to clarify that dashboard GPS navigation systems were exempt from the state ban on television screens visible to drivers. The Senate had passed its measure in June 2004, while an Assembly counterpart remained pending. State Police representatives described spoken navigation as useful and relatively undistracting; Public Citizen urged federal scrutiny of in-vehicle screens as potential distractions.

news.headline: Merritt traffic still finding ‘Waze’ through New Canaan local streets
news.factual_summary: New Canaan residents asked the Police Commission to address commuter traffic leaving the Merritt Parkway and using residential streets. At a September 19 meeting, residents described speeding, stop-sign violations and safety concerns. A traffic engineer presented Nursery Road counts from June 2017. Police continued studying possible measures and increased morning enforcement, while commissioners considered whether turn restrictions would shift traffic to neighboring streets.

news.headline: Bay Area Freeway Patrol Joins Waze Connected Citizens Program
news.factual_summary: The Bay Area Metropolitan Transportation Commission entered a Waze data partnership involving its Freeway Service Patrol. User incident reports would help patrol tow drivers detect problems, while patrol reports of crashes and stalled vehicles would be supplied to Waze. Officials anticipated more timely assistance and better traffic information.

news.headline: Waymo Robotaxis Have A New Job: Spotting Potholes
news.factual_summary: Waymo and Waze announced a pilot sharing robotaxi pothole detections with city and state transportation agencies through Waze for Cities and with app users. Drivers could verify detections alongside existing user reports. Initial coverage included the Bay Area, Los Angeles, Phoenix, Austin and Atlanta, with about 500 potholes identified. Expansion into cities affected by winter freeze-thaw damage was planned.

news.headline: Louisville Announces Real-Time Traffic App
news.factual_summary: Louisville announced a Waze partnership and said it was sending road-closure information directly to the app, alongside user-submitted incident reports. Officials described using the service to notify travelers about construction, crashes and special events and to support routes around closures.

news.headline: SCHUMER LAUNCHES MAJOR PUSH TO PREVENT BRIDGE STRIKES THAT HAVE PLAGUED WESTCHESTER COUNTY FOR DECADES; SENATOR CALLS ON LEADING GPS DEVELOPERS TO INTEGRATE DATA WARNING COMMERCIAL VEHICLE DRIVERS OF ROAD RESTRICTIONS, PROMOTE DRIVER SAFETY and DECREASE TRAFFIC Currently, GPS Applications--Google Maps, Apple Maps and Waze--Do Not Contain Data Warning Commercial Drivers Of Roadway Restrictions Such As Maximum Vehicle Height; In The Last Decade, The King Street Bridge In Westchester County Has Been Struck ~150 Times Sen. Schumer, Charles E. - (D - NY ) News Release
news.factual_summary: Senator Chuck Schumer, joined by Richard Blumenthal and Ed Markey, urged Google, Apple and Waze to warn commercial drivers about roadway height, weight and other restrictions. Schumer cited repeated bridge strikes on Westchester parkways, including nearly 150 at King Street Bridge over a decade. The senators proposed allowing users to identify commercial vehicles so navigation apps could flag restricted routes.

news.headline: NYPD Sends Letter To Google Demanding It Remove Cop Checkpoint Notifications From Google Maps
news.factual_summary: Techdirt criticized the NYPD’s demand that Google remove police-checkpoint notifications, arguing that such information also helps sober drivers avoid stops and delays. The article quoted the department’s warning that posting checkpoint locations could impede enforcement, Google’s defense of safety alerts and a Mothers Against Drunk Driving representative’s comments about advance publicity. It questioned the department’s rationale for restricting the reports.

news.headline: PORT AUTHORITY, WAZE NAVIGATION APP PARTNER FOR REAL-TIME TRAFFIC DATA SHARING
news.factual_summary: The Port Authority of New York and New Jersey announced a free Waze data partnership covering its bridges, tunnels, terminals and access roads. The agency would combine user reports with cameras and sensors and send lane closures and incidents to the app. Officials anticipated better alerts, modeling and traffic management. A Waze representative said the partnership was already helping drivers near Port Authority facilities.

news.headline: Navigation app helps arm Los Angeles drivers against "Carmageddon"
news.factual_summary: Waze and Los Angeles broadcaster KABC planned to combine crowdsourced traffic information, cameras and reporting during the July 2011 closure of Interstate 405. The article describes alternate-route information and questions whether television coverage would reach drivers already traveling or visiting tourists.

news.headline: Traffic apps cause headache for cities Shortcuts on Waze, Google Maps clog streets
news.factual_summary: A news feature examined conflicts between navigation-app shortcuts and neighborhood traffic planning. Fremont introduced rush-hour turn restrictions and shared them with Waze; its engineer said the changes helped but might displace traffic elsewhere. Boston used Waze data for signal timing. Waze said Boston’s use of its data helped reduce congestion by 18% month over month.

news.headline: Applied Information Integrates School Zone Safety Beacons, Emergency Vehicles and Other Traffic Control Devices into Waze to Improve Roadway Safety The Waze for Cities program enables local transportation agencies with Applied Information technology to provide additional free, automatic safety alerts
news.factual_summary: Applied Information announced that connected school-zone beacons, emergency vehicles at incident scenes and malfunctioning traffic signals could automatically post alerts in Waze. The integration uses its TravelSafely technology and the Waze for Cities data-sharing program. Local transportation agencies with compatible infrastructure and vehicles could participate without charge. The company described the alerts as a way to warn drivers about active school zones, responders and signal problems.

news.headline: Waze's growth chief: Commuters, even robots need a better route Under-the-radar app is beloved by users -- and a few celebrities
news.factual_summary: A USA Today profile described Waze’s combination of driver location data, volunteer map editing, advertising and government partnerships. Growth chief Di-Ann Eisnor said the goal was better traffic management and shorter commutes; Boston officials described using its information alongside other sources. The article also discussed possible roles in autonomous driving.

news.headline: MIAMI-DADE TRANSIT AND WAZE CARPOOL JOIN FORCES TO ALLEVIATE CONGESTION
news.factual_summary: Miami-Dade’s transportation department partnered with Waze Carpool to offer free rides throughout the county from September 23–27, followed by a $2 flat fare starting September 28. Officials aimed to encourage shared commuting and connections to Metrorail, including designated carpool spaces at Dadeland North. The app matched drivers and riders by route and schedule, with profile-based preferences.

news.headline: Waze, ABC team to help L.A. drivers navigate traffic nightmare
news.factual_summary: KABC and Waze partnered ahead of Los Angeles’s planned Interstate 405 closure to provide traffic updates and alternate-route information from smartphone users. The report describes planning before departure and changing conditions during travel, while noting undisclosed financial terms and possible broadcaster revenue opportunities.

news.headline: Boston, Google partner on AI-based traffic signal optimization
news.factual_summary: Boston partnered with Google Project Green Light to analyze traffic and adjust signal timing. Engineers reviewed AI-generated recommendations for safety, feasibility and effectiveness before implementing four changes in Fenway-Kenmore, Mission Hill and Jamaica Plain. The city reported stop-and-go traffic reductions exceeding 50% at two intersections and said ongoing measurements would guide additional adjustments.

news.headline: The traffic calming illusion
news.factual_summary: A republished Connecticut transportation column discussed GPS-driven neighborhood cut-through traffic and physical traffic-calming tools, including speed tables, roundabouts, chicanes, curb extensions and sidewalks. The author argued that signs alone are ineffective and that neighborhood measures depend on functioning arterial routes. The column criticized approaches that merely shift congestion between streets without addressing broader planning.

news.headline: Letter Demands Google Stops Telling Waze Users About NYPD Activity
news.factual_summary: The NYPD sent Google a cease-and-desist letter demanding an end to sharing sobriety-checkpoint information in Waze. The department argued that users posting locations could interfere with enforcement and help impaired drivers evade detection. Google defended police-location alerts as promoting safer driving. The article discussed possible responses, including removing features, declining the request or facing a lawsuit.

news.headline: DEC. 2 HOLIDAY PARADESROAD CLOSURES, ONE-WAY TRAFFIC PATTERN AND EXTENDED PEDESTRIAN ZONE
news.factual_summary: Alexandria planned road closures, parking restrictions and traffic changes for its December 2, 2023 Scottish Christmas Walk and Holiday Boat Parade of Lights. Union Street would become northbound-only between Duke and Queen streets around 3 p.m., while King Street’s pedestrian zone would expand and nearby vehicle access would be limited. The city recommended Waze for navigating closures and urged businesses to plan deliveries around the events.

news.headline: Traffic-weary homeowners and Waze are at war, again
news.factual_summary: Residents in several U.S. communities complained that navigation apps were directing heavy cut-through traffic onto local streets during construction or congestion. Takoma Park resident Timothy Connor said his false Waze incident reports had little effect and his account was blocked. Officials elsewhere used turn restrictions or barriers; Waze defended routing on legal streets and said false reports self-correct.

news.headline: Waze Launches International Partner Program Enabling Local Map-Owners Worldwide to Convert Static Maps Into Live, Navigable Maps
news.factual_summary: Waze announced a partnership program for local map providers worldwide, offering to combine their base maps with crowdsourced road updates and traffic information. The company said GPS traces and user reports could help build navigable maps, including turn restrictions and historical speeds. It expected to announce its first partnerships in January 2010, with discussions under way in South America and East Asia. Waze said crowdsourced updates could lower map-maintenance costs and keep road information current.

news.headline: ALK releases new CoPilot Truck navigation
news.factual_summary: ALK announced updated CoPilot Truck navigation for smartphones, tablets, laptops and rugged devices. The report describes offline maps, vehicle-specific routing, alternate routes and RouteSync integration intended to align dispatch plans with in-cab directions. ALK said the update would help drivers follow truck restrictions and dispatch plans.

news.headline: Google Maps will now help travelers find the most eco-friendly route
news.factual_summary: Google was releasing Maps features to identify fuel-efficient driving routes and provide cyclists with route details through lite navigation. The article also describes bike and scooter availability information being introduced in 300 cities, including Berlin, New York and São Paulo, and flight-specific and seat-specific emissions estimates in Google Flights. Google estimated potential annual emissions savings of more than one million tons from fuel-efficient routing.

news.headline: Google Maps Can Now Remember Which Route You Prefer
news.factual_summary: Android Headlines reported that Google Maps was beginning to retain route-option settings such as avoiding highways, tolls and ferries, reducing the need to reset them for later trips. Users would need to change those settings when they wanted different options. The article said full rollout timing was unclear.

news.headline: Google Assistant launches on Waze so you can yell at your car about traffic
news.factual_summary: Google Assistant became available in Waze for Android users in English. The update allowed drivers to use voice commands to avoid tolls, search for places along a route and check traffic conditions. Google said the integration aimed to reduce distractions by letting users interact without handling their phones.

news.headline: How to add a stop to your route on Waze and edit the path you're driving
news.factual_summary: The guide described adding an intermediate stop to a Waze route through the navigation options. Users could choose parking, gas or food suggestions, or search for a custom address, then accept the recalculated route. The article said only one stop could be added at a time and recommended beginning a new route to change the final destination.

news.headline: 'What is Waze?': How to navigate the socially-focused traffic and navigation app
news.factual_summary: The article introduced Waze as a free, community-based navigation app using driver reports to display traffic, crashes, hazards and police activity. It described route choices, toll avoidance, ETA sharing, incident comments, messaging, music and calendar connections. It also explained map editors’ role in checking contributed information and the points and achievement system used to encourage participation.

news.headline: Hey Google Show Me the Map or Report a Pothole in Waze
news.factual_summary: Google announced Assistant voice controls in Waze for English-speaking Android users. Drivers could report traffic and potholes, check alternate routes, avoid tolls, make calls, send messages and control media without leaving the navigation screen. Google said voice commands were intended to help drivers keep their attention on the road.

news.headline: Why Navigation Apps, Working Properly, Can Make Traffic Flows Worse -- And What To Do About It
news.factual_summary: Drawing on Jane Macfarlane’s IEEE Spectrum analysis, Glyn Moody argued that navigation apps optimizing individual journeys could overload residential streets and disrupt wider traffic flows. He discussed local responses including false incident reports, speed bumps and access restrictions. Moody advocated sharing aggregated traffic data among navigation providers and city engineers, with privacy protections, to support coordinated routing and traffic management.

news.headline: A man walked down a street with 99 phones in a wagon. Google Maps thought it was a traffic jam.
news.factual_summary: Berlin artist Simon Weckert staged a project in which an assistant pulled a wagon carrying 99 smartphones along mostly empty streets. His video showed Google Maps marking those streets as congested. Weckert said the work explored trust in navigation services and their influence on cities. Google said traffic information drew on multiple continuously updated sources and welcomed creative tests that could help improve its maps.

news.headline: Enough with the speed traps
news.factual_summary: CNN contributor Ruben Navarrette defended Waze’s user-reported police-location alerts against law-enforcement objections about officer safety. He argued that concerns also reflected lost speeding-ticket revenue and cited court cases protecting warnings about police presence. Waze said the alerts encouraged careful driving.

news.headline: Local Residents In LA Reporting Fake Traffic Accidents In Attempt To Reroute Waze Drivers
news.factual_summary: An Android Headlines article, drawing on Associated Press reporting, described Los Angeles residents’ complaints about Waze directing commuters through previously quiet neighborhoods. It said residents were submitting false accident reports to discourage through traffic. A company spokeswoman said subsequent drivers’ data would negate such reports.

news.headline: INRIX Traffic Powers ALK’s CoPilot Live Smartphone Navigation in North America
news.factual_summary: INRIX and ALK Technologies announced real-time traffic information for CoPilot Live v8 smartphone navigation in North America. The release said Windows Mobile and Android customers could purchase it immediately, while iPhone availability was planned before the end of 2009. CoPilot stored maps on the phone and displayed incident and congestion updates. The companies said the service could help drivers plan around delays and reduce fuel use.

news.headline: L.A. Council Seeks Solutions To Waze Traffic On Side Streets
news.factual_summary: The Los Angeles City Council unanimously approved a proposal to address navigation apps directing traffic onto residential streets. The Transportation Committee recommended that LADOT lead negotiations on data sharing with app companies. Councilman Paul Krekorian sought cooperation to reduce neighborhood traffic hazards. Related proposals included reviewing possible legal action against Waze and coordinating with developers to keep drivers out of wildfire evacuation areas.

news.headline: Google 's Waze goes hands-free with new voice command and gets motorcycle mode for tailored navigation
news.factual_summary: Waze introduced motorcycle mode and hands-free commands on Android and iOS. Motorcycle mode used riders’ traffic data to tailor routes and arrival estimates, while the OK Waze command let users enter destinations, report incidents and request updated arrival times. Voice support initially operated in English, with additional languages planned. The article also noted Spotify integration and the app’s existing speed alerts.

news.headline: Sidewalk Labs will launch Flow a smart traffic and parking platform in Columbus , Ohio
news.factual_summary: A technology article described Sidewalk Labs’ proposed Flow demonstration in Columbus, combining transport information and parking data to guide trips, locate spaces and support variable pricing. The offer included software access and Wi-Fi kiosks over three years. Sidewalk projected parking revenue and enforcement gains, while an outside researcher questioned variable-pricing benefits.

news.headline: BLOG: Opinion Northwest: The case for reducing a lane on Dexter Avenue North
news.factual_summary: A Seattle Times opinion writer advocated reducing Dexter Avenue North between Mercer Street and Denny Way from four lanes to three, including a center turn lane. Citing cycling injuries, speeding and city studies of other road diets, the writer argued the change could improve cyclist and pedestrian safety. A city engineer said the segment was scheduled for study the following year.

news.headline: Angry dustups on New Canaan's Nursery Road
news.factual_summary: New Canaan officials reported drivers ignoring a morning left-turn restriction from Marvin Ridge Road onto Nursery Road, a shortcut around Merritt Parkway congestion. Residents described confrontations, and police observed drivers using private driveways to turn around. Police notified Waze, Google Maps, TomTom and other services of the restriction and continued collecting traffic data while enforcing the turn ban.

news.headline: News roundup, Jan. 16: Senators call for more truck info on phone GPS apps; new standard coating from suspension maker; on-truck vid system integrates third-party telematics
news.factual_summary: Senators Richard Blumenthal, Chuck Schumer and Ed Markey urged Google, Apple and Waze to add height, weight and other truck restrictions to smartphone navigation apps. They sought to keep commercial vehicles off restricted parkways and prevent low-bridge collisions. Connecticut trucking representative Joseph Sculley supported the request, saying out-of-state drivers might use general navigation apps instead of truck-specific systems.

news.headline: U.S. Xpress Drivers Get 'CoPilot'
news.factual_summary: U.S. Xpress Enterprises planned to install ALK Technologies’ CoPilot Truck navigation software throughout its fleet of more than 5,000 tractors.
