The Chattanooga carrier said the system would provide spoken turn-by-turn directions in the United States and Canada, avoid roads and structures with truck restrictions, and recalculate routes after disruptions or wrong turns. Management cited directions as a major driver concern and described internal testing.

news.headline: Five Apps for That: Don’t get delayed by bad directions
news.factual_summary: A trucking guide compared CoPilot, MyOne20, SmartTruck Route, Sygic Truck GPS and TruckMap. It described vehicle profiles accounting for dimensions, weight and hazardous materials, alongside app-specific features such as offline maps, multistop planning, traffic information, toll avoidance, mileage logs and truck-service locations. The guide listed free and subscription options and noted that TruckMap’s Android release was still expected.

news.headline: ALK Technologies Introduces PC*MILER Navigator 430
news.factual_summary: ALK Technologies announced the PC*MILER Navigator 430, a portable GPS device for truck drivers in the United States and Canada. The release describes spoken directions, vehicle-size settings, truck restrictions, route recalculation, multistop planning and trip-cost estimates. It lists a $349 suggested price and availability through truck stops. ALK said the device could reduce avoidable mileage and help drivers account for truck restrictions.

news.headline: Webtech Wireless Forms Navigation Partnership with ALK Technologies
news.factual_summary: Webtech Wireless announced version 2.5 of its MDT 3100 in-cab terminal with ALK Technologies’ CoPilot Truck navigation, available for immediate delivery. Drivers could configure routes for vehicle dimensions and cargo restrictions. The release also added driver provisioning, automatic driver changes and cross-border hours-of-service support.

news.headline: TeleType Releases First Server Based Truck Routing App for Android Smartphones
news.factual_summary: TeleType released SmartTruckRoute for Android, describing server-based truck routing, traffic information and routes tailored to vehicle dimensions, loads and hazardous-material restrictions. iPhone and iPad versions and freight-load information were planned additions.

news.headline: State looks to avoid GPS sending drivers down small roads
news.factual_summary: Connecticut lawmakers were considering a proposal to direct navigation systems toward state-maintained roads rather than small local streets during diversions. Newtown police chief David Kullgren and Representative Mitch Bolinsky described neighborhood congestion caused by highway backups and app routing. The article also recounts Newtown’s conversion of Hall Lane to one-way traffic, which officials said reduced through traffic after studies and planning.

news.headline: Torrance Fire Department Introduces Traffic Safety Digital Alert
news.factual_summary: Torrance Fire Department announced a rollout of HAAS Alert’s Safety Cloud to send drivers digital warnings when emergency vehicles are nearby. Notifications supplement lights and sirens through Waze, Apple Maps and supported vehicle displays. Fire officials said warnings can arrive up to 30 seconds ahead and described the system as a way to lower collision risk for responders and motorists.

news.headline: SmartTruckRoute app now offers route optimization
news.factual_summary: TeleType announced SmartTruckDispatch, a web service that lets fleet managers sequence delivery stops and send routes to drivers using SmartTruckRoute. Managers could enter or upload stops, while the app applied truck dimensions and restrictions for navigation. The dispatch service was free when recipient drivers had paid app subscriptions. TeleType said the service could improve route planning and help drivers avoid restricted roads.

news.headline: Ferguson hopes speed humps slow down vehicles Drivers cut through Ferguson at up to 80 mph. The city hopes speed humps will slow them down.
news.factual_summary: Ferguson began a $262,000 project installing 109 speed humps on 45 residential roads after residents’ complaints and nearly two years of traffic monitoring. Officials said some drivers used neighborhood streets to bypass major roads and reached speeds as high as 80 mph. Locations were chosen using the collected data, with completion expected by October and additional humps under consideration for the following year.

news.headline: Mount Prospect mulling traffic calming in popular cut-through neighborhood
news.factual_summary: Mount Prospect was finishing a three-week trial of traffic-calming devices on residential cut-through routes. Temporary cones, bollards and rubber curbs were installed while staff collected speed data and resident feedback. Some residents described longstanding speeding and heavy-vehicle problems but opposed making the devices permanent, suggesting other controls. Results were to go before the Transportation Safety Commission before any permanent decision.

news.headline: SLOWING DOWN FOR SAFETY: HOW CHESAPEAKE'S TRAFFIC CALMING PROGRAM WORKS
news.factual_summary: Chesapeake explains how residents can request traffic calming on qualifying residential streets. The program begins with speed studies, then temporary radar feedback signs and possible permanent signage. If excessive speeds persist, physical measures may follow after a year, subject to resident approval and other requirements. The city describes eligibility criteria and a staged process for evaluating and addressing neighborhood speeding.

news.headline: TRAFFIC-CALMING INSTALLED ON SHADY AVE.
news.factual_summary: Pittsburgh installed four speed tables, pavement markings and signs on Shady Avenue after a resident-requested traffic study found widespread speeding. The March 2024 study recorded 97% of vehicles above the 25 mph limit and an average near 34 mph. Officials described the work as part of Vision Zero and intended to improve safety for people traveling through the neighborhood.

news.headline: CITY INSTALLING TRAFFIC-CALMING MEASURES
news.factual_summary: Pittsburgh began installing five speed tables, markings and signs on Southern Avenue in Mount Washington after a resident-requested study found widespread speeding. The 2022 study recorded 75% of drivers above the 25 mph limit and 15% above 35 mph. Officials expected the work to finish Friday and described it as another neighborhood Vision Zero investment.

news.headline: MAKING YOUR STREETS SAFER: TRAFFIC CALMING COMING TO 141 LOCATIONS ACROSS SAN FRANCISCO
news.factual_summary: San Francisco's transportation agency planned to begin installing traffic-calming devices at 141 resident-requested locations on November 20, 2025, with completion expected by February, weather permitting. Devices included speed humps, cushions and tables. The agency had paused new applications while completing approved work and said another 14 locations would receive devices under a separate spring contract.

news.headline: Crews hit streets to fill 'traffic calming' requests
news.factual_summary: San Francisco crews began traffic-calming work at 141 locations as the transportation agency addressed a backlog of resident requests. New applications remained suspended after demand exceeded staff capacity. The agency said it had installed more than 850 devices since 2021 and was building projects approved in fiscal 2022 while designing later approvals. Neighborhood representatives described continuing requests for safer intersections and crossings.

news.headline: Will speed humps, stop signs solve this neighborhood's traffic issue?
news.factual_summary: Mount Prospect's village board approved temporary speed humps on Audrey Lane and Hatlen Avenue in Hatlen Heights, along with a four-way stop, pavement markings, no-truck signs and a curb bump-out. The humps were planned for spring installation and fall removal before evaluation. Trustees rejected small traffic circles and additional stop signs following debate over speeding, cut-through traffic and parking.

news.headline: Get up to speed on Capital Region speed humps
news.factual_summary: Albany writer Jim Crowe used a fictional interview with the head of an invented speed-hump institute to satirize growing use of traffic-calming devices in the Capital Region. The exchange jokes about closely spaced humps, displaced traffic, speed-camera revenue, emergency access and riders using humps as jumps. It concludes with a fictional proposal to place speed humps in roundabouts.

news.headline: Des Moines may add dozens more speed humps to these residential streets
news.factual_summary: Des Moines City Council was scheduled to vote on approximately 40 additional residential speed humps for the following year. Proposed locations included stretches of 23rd, Center, Cottage Grove, East Douglas, Hull, Southwest 14th and Williams/East 42nd streets. The proposal followed continuing speeding complaints and traffic deaths, alongside debate about vehicle damage, emergency-response delays and diversion to neighboring streets.

news.headline: DETROIT ANNOUNCES 2026 SPEED HUMP PROGRAM LIST: 312 NEW HUMPS PLANNED FOR SAFER NEIGHBORHOODS
news.factual_summary: Detroit planned 312 additional residential speed humps in 2026 and gave residents on listed streets until April 24 to opt out. Public Works said earlier approved locations delayed by utility or resurfacing work would receive priority. Selection criteria included speeding and crash records, proximity to schools and parks, cut-through traffic and resident support. The city reported 11,412 humps installed since 2016.

news.headline: Godfrey tables Levis Lane speed hump debate for traffic study
news.factual_summary: Godfrey's Public Safety Committee postponed a decision on competing petitions to retain or remove a Levis Lane speed hump pending a traffic study. Residents disagreed about its effectiveness, while the mayor and village engineer favored keeping it. The village attorney said neither petition met signature requirements. Officials planned to measure traffic volumes and speeds before further action.

news.headline: East Lampeter officials move forward on traffic safety issues, consider speed bumps near Costco
news.factual_summary: East Lampeter supervisors considered temporary speed bumps on Enfield Drive after a study found more than 1,000 daily vehicles on the residential shortcut near Costco. They approved center and edge lines on Clover Heights Road to clarify access near Noel's Cafe, plus a budget amendment for signal and sign repairs. Speed-bump costs remained under investigation, with no installation approved.

news.headline: How Abington residents can request devices to slow traffic
news.factual_summary: Abington adopted a policy allowing residents or the township manager to initiate traffic-calming reviews. Eligible streets must meet traffic, speed and road-type criteria, with studies and resident petitions required for owner-led requests. Possible devices include humps, narrowing and chicanes. The article described earlier studies finding varied levels of enforceable speeding and noted potential noise and other tradeoffs.

news.headline: Bill would // relinquish // control of // speed humps St. Louis alderman wants out of speed hump business
news.factual_summary: St. Louis Alderman Michael Browning introduced a bill requiring staff approval for new speed humps and allowing rejection of requests outside city criteria. It would broaden requests to neighborhood associations, police captains and petitioning residents and publicly list approved projects awaiting funding. The proposal accompanied a planned transition toward centralized transportation management by 2029.

news.headline: Alderman wants out of speed hump business St. Louis alderman wants out of speed hump business
news.factual_summary: St. Louis Alderman Michael Browning proposed returning speed-hump decisions to professional staff, allowing rejection of requests that fail design or traffic-calming guidelines. Aldermen, neighborhood groups, police captains and petitioning residents could still request devices. The bill would list approved but unfunded projects publicly and accompany broader changes toward a centralized transportation department.

news.headline: HOWARD COUNTY DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC WORKS TO HOST COMMUNITY OUTREACH OPEN HOUSE ON THE DEEPAGE DRIVE AND RUSTLING LEAF TRAFFIC CALMING PROJECT
news.factual_summary: Howard County scheduled an October 21 open house in Columbia to present proposed traffic calming on Deepage Drive and Rustling Leaf. Plans call for speed humps and signs on Deepage Drive and a raised intersection on Rustling Leaf under the county’s updated neighborhood policy. Public works staff will answer questions and collect feedback, with emailed comments accepted through November 5, 2026.

news.headline: Town beset by traffic via navigation apps closes off streets
news.factual_summary: Leonia, New Jersey, began restricting nonresident commuter traffic on roughly 60 residential streets near the George Washington Bridge. Residents could display yellow access tags, and police planned warnings followed by $200 tickets. Police Chief Thomas Rowe said Waze had updated routes and described extensive traffic studies. Some residents welcomed lighter traffic, while a motorists’ advocate questioned the restrictions’ legality.

news.headline: Illinois Bill Requires Posting of Truck Routes and Education on Truck GPS Illinois Public Act 97-0291 Takes Effect January 1, 2012
news.factual_summary: A Rand McNally release reported that Illinois Governor Pat Quinn signed legislation requiring local truck-route reporting, online access through the state transportation department and driver education about truck-specific GPS. The law was scheduled to take effect January 1, 2012, following task-force recommendations. Supporters said the law would improve truck routing and reduce bridge strikes.

news.headline: Gov. Wolf Announces Partnership With Waze Connected Citizens Program to Improve Traveler Information PennDOT Modernizes Traffic Management Through New Data Exchange Partnership
news.factual_summary: Pennsylvania Governor Tom Wolf announced a free two-way partnership between PennDOT and Waze. The agency would provide road-condition reports to the app and receive crowdsourced incidents and slowdown information to supplement internal traffic monitoring. Officials anticipated improved traveler information and quicker awareness of congestion.

news.headline: SmartTruckRoute Truck Routing App Now Offers Voice Navigation
news.factual_summary: TeleType added spoken turn-by-turn instructions and a navigation panel to SmartTruckRoute for Android. The release describes vehicle-specific routes, restrictions and live information, with Apple-device versions and freight-load modules still planned. TeleType said voice guidance would support hands-free use.

news.headline: SmartTruckRoute Truck Routing App Now with Lifetime Free Updates: Update Also Offers Enhanced Navigation Display and Routing, and New Data Usage Conservation Mode
news.factual_summary: TeleType updated SmartTruckRoute for Android with revised displays and routing, a cellular-data conservation mode and an October lifetime-service offer. The release describes server-based routes using truck dimensions and restrictions, voice guidance and live information. An iOS version remained in development.

news.headline: SmartTruckRoute Truck Routing App Now Available for iPhone, iPad, Android
news.factual_summary: TeleType announced on February 22, 2013 that SmartTruckRoute was available for iPhone and iPad alongside its Android version. The app uses remote servers and phone GPS to generate routes based on truck dimensions, restrictions and hazardous-material requirements, with spoken directions and updated restriction data. TeleType said restriction data was updated daily and incorporated driver feedback.

news.headline: Webtech Wireless Announces Navigation Partnership With ALK Tech - Quick Facts
news.factual_summary: Webtech Wireless announced version 2.5 of its MDT 3100 in-cab terminal with ALK Technologies’ CoPilot Truck navigation, available for immediate delivery. Drivers could configure routes for vehicle dimensions and cargo restrictions. The release also added driver provisioning, automatic driver changes and cross-border hours-of-service support.

news.headline: SmartTruckRoute Truck GPS App Offers Android and iPhone Users Instant Truck Navigation and Free Updates
news.factual_summary: TeleType announced updated SmartTruckRoute apps for Android and iPhone with faster routing, alternatives, multiple waypoints, speed alerts and axle-weight settings. The subscription service used truck restrictions, daily server updates and driver feedback, with truck-related locations and fuel prices. The company promoted avoidance of tickets and safer navigation.

news.headline: TeleType Android truck routing app
news.factual_summary: A product brief described TeleType’s released SmartTruckRoute Android application, offering truck-specific routes, traffic displays and directions based on vehicle dimensions and restrictions. It also mentioned voice destination entry and hazardous-material settings. Apple-device versions and future freight-load modules were still planned.

news.headline: Truck navigation adds iPhone, iPad
news.factual_summary: ALK described version 8 of CoPilot Live Truck for mobile devices, including an iPhone and iPad application. The report outlines on-device truck maps, voice guidance, vehicle dimensions, restriction-aware routing, lane information, map updates and mileage or fuel-cost tools. It says the product would be available in May 2010, although its opening also calls the application available.

news.headline: Let’s build giant tree circles in every Seattle neighborhood
news.factual_summary: Tom Fucoloro proposed turning selected Seattle residential intersections into spaces for large publicly owned trees, walking, cycling and small neighborhood parks. His February 25, 2025 essay suggests blocking through-driving where neighborhood routes meet, while retaining pedestrian and bicycle paths. He cites existing tree-filled traffic circles and a Capitol Hill diverter as precedents, and argues that the concept could combine traffic calming, stormwater retention and tree-canopy expansion.

news.headline: Seattle Is Finally Getting Its First Protected Intersection
news.factual_summary: Seattle’s transportation department had begun soliciting bids for Thomas Street improvements that would include a protected intersection at Dexter Avenue North. The July 6, 2023 report describes corner buffers and a diverter intended to separate walking and cycling from vehicle traffic. Following budget reductions, a quick-build plaza near Fifth Avenue North would replace a more permanent design and block through-driving. Installation was expected that fall, subject to delays.

news.headline: Alerts caution drivers to move
news.factual_summary: Illinois State Police and the state technology department partnered with HAAS Alert to expand move-over warnings to supported vehicle displays. Police send location information about incidents or other hazards to Safety Cloud, which alerts approaching drivers to slow down and change lanes. The initiative builds on existing Waze and Google Maps alerts and is intended to protect roadside troopers and drivers.

news.headline: VIRGINIA BEACH NAMED AMONG 2021 SMART 50 AWARD RECIPIENTS
news.factual_summary: Virginia Beach won a 2021 Smart 50 Award for its Waze traffic-data partnership. The city described sharing real-time road-condition information to support driver routing and official responses to traffic and weather incidents. It said the initiative continued adding data sources and app integrations. An October awards ceremony in Washington was planned alongside the Smart Cities Connect Conference.

news.headline: ILLINOIS DEPARTMENT OF INNOVATION & TECHNOLOGY RECEIVES RECOGNITION FOR ENHANCING PUBLIC SAFETY THROUGH TECHNOLOGY
news.factual_summary: Illinois’ technology department received a 2025 Government Experience Project Award for its Move Over Illinois real-time alert program. Developed with Google and Illinois State Police, the project began sending Waze warnings in 2024 about crashes, hazards and roadside incidents. Officials described the award as recognition of work intended to improve driver awareness and protect responders.

news.headline: Greenwich votes to add 25 MPH speed limits to three roads
news.factual_summary: Greenwich selectmen voted November 14 to establish 25 mph limits on Woodland Drive, Will Merry Lane and Spring House Road, subject to state transportation approval. Residents had raised concerns about speeding and cut-through traffic, including drivers following navigation apps around Merritt Parkway congestion. Town staff conducted traffic studies before recommending limits, with Woodland Drive averaging about 400 vehicles daily.

news.headline: Science & Technology Directorate: QuickRoute Navigation App Now Available for First Responders
news.factual_summary: DHS announced commercial availability of QuickRoute, an iOS navigation app developed with Azimuth1 for first responders. The agency said it considered emergency-vehicle dimensions, turning limits, hazards and special traffic rules. A civilian version was free, while emergency-service access required a developer code and cost about $10 monthly. Agencies were invited to test the app and a dispatcher component for sending destinations.

news.headline: CITY OF ATLANTA JOINS WAZE CONNECTED CITIZEN PROGRAM
news.factual_summary: Atlanta announced participation in Waze’s free Connected Citizens data-sharing program. The city would provide construction, crash and road-closure information and receive anonymous user incident and slowdown reports. Officials intended to use the data to assess road conditions and inform congestion measures alongside other transport initiatives.

news.headline: L.A. City Councilman Wants Legal Action Against Waze
news.factual_summary: Los Angeles councilmember David Ryu asked the city attorney to examine legal action against Waze, citing heavy traffic, accidents and neighborhood disruption in Sherman Oaks Hills. The report also described Paul Krekorian’s request to review data-sharing arrangements and potential collision liability, and Paul Koretz’s proposal to prevent navigation into evacuation areas. The lawmakers sought legal review and coordination with app operators.

news.headline: Fire Dept. and NYU aim to cut response times
news.factual_summary: FDNY and New York University began a year-long partnership to study traffic patterns and use AI to improve emergency-resource placement and response times. Commissioner Laura Kavanagh said NYU brought expertise and access to additional datasets, including Waze information. The project follows slower response times and increased call volumes, with funding of $90,000 from the U.S. Transportation Department and $56,000 in FDNY personnel costs.

news.headline: Move over! Two map apps to notify drivers when state police are stopped ahead
news.factual_summary: Illinois State Police launched real-time roadside alerts through Waze, with Google Maps support planned in the coming weeks. Trooper locations at crashes, stops and assistance calls would pass through Google’s cloud service to warn approaching drivers. Officials said the program aims to prevent move-over crashes and initially covers state troopers, with the alerts kept separate from decisions about enforcement.

news.headline: Waymo robotaxis have a side hustle: Reporting potholes
news.factual_summary: Waymo and Waze piloted pothole detection using autonomous-vehicle sensors in San Francisco, Los Angeles, Phoenix, Atlanta and Austin. Public agencies would access the data through Waze for Cities, while app users received alerts and could verify hazards. Waymo reported roughly 500 detections. The article described the data as complementing municipal 311 reports, manual inspections and other technology-based detection methods.

news.headline: CITY OF ATLANTA LAUNCHES COMMUTEATL WEBSITE
news.factual_summary: Atlanta launched CommuteATL to help travelers during reconstruction of the I-85 bridge. The map combined Waze alerts and speeds with MARTA and streetcar schedules, parking information and Relay Bike Share stations. The city encouraged transit, telecommuting and shared rides, restricted non-local traffic in selected neighborhoods, and increased traffic-management staffing. Engineers would adjust signals to keep traffic on major roads, while the team planned further mapping features.

news.headline: AH Primetime: Waze's Role In Google 's Autonomous Cars
news.factual_summary: An Android Headlines commentary considered whether Waze’s municipal data partnerships could help Google develop and secure approval for autonomous vehicles. It described limited self-driving tests, regulatory obstacles and Waze’s Tel Aviv commuter-ride trial. Waze denied that its government agreements were directly helping Google at that time.

news.headline: House Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on Digital Commerce and Consumer Protection Hearing "Disrupter Series: Smart Communities." Testimony by Kyle Chisek, Director of Bureau Relations, City of Portland , Oregon , Office of Mayor Ted Wheeler
news.factual_summary: In congressional testimony, Portland official Kyle Chisek described transport collaborations, open-data work and TriMet’s grant-funded effort to integrate multiple travel modes into trip planning. He said Portland was supplying Waze with street closures and working toward safer school routes and Vision Zero goals.

news.headline: Guest Commentary: Solution for Mace is to Regulate Traffic at Mace and Montgomery
news.factual_summary: Jason Taormino argued that navigation apps were diverting Interstate 80 commuters through Davis and worsening congestion on Mace Boulevard and other local roads. He proposed a temporary signal at Mace and Montgomery to meter incoming traffic and keep queues outside neighborhoods. He also criticized lane reductions and bicycle-oriented street changes, drawing on his experiences driving around the city.

news.headline: Maine , New Hampshire & Vermont Join 'Waze'
news.factual_summary: Transportation agencies in Maine, New Hampshire and Vermont jointly announced a Waze Connected Citizens partnership. The states would share sensor feeds, closures, construction and other traffic information, while Waze would return public incident and closure reports. Officials expected more timely regional information for travelers and emergency responders.

news.headline: Navigating through the “new normal" of travel and infrastructure as cities reopen
news.factual_summary: Waze public-partnerships executive Andrew Stober urged cities to shape travel choices as pandemic restrictions eased. He discussed bus lanes, fare discounts, congestion-pricing proposals and data tools, arguing that renewed driving could undermine climate and equity goals. The article promoted carpool matching and employer programs as near-term options for access to jobs while larger transit investments took time.

news.headline: Google Maps puts out a new feature to make driving a little easier
news.factual_summary: Google Maps added community reports for crashes, speed traps, slow traffic, construction, lane closures, disabled vehicles and objects in the road. Users could select the plus button and add a report. The article recalled NYPD concerns about checkpoint alerts and quoted a department spokesperson saying discussions with Google sought safer driving without obstructing enforcement.

news.headline: What are the environmental pros and cons of so many of us relying on GPS apps
news.factual_summary: EarthTalk examined how GPS routing could save individual drivers time while shifting congestion onto residential streets. It cited University of California traffic simulations in which app-guided diversions created queues at freeway exits and neighborhood intersections. The column discussed residents’ concerns about cut-through traffic and Google’s planned lower-fuel routing feature as an attempt to account for environmental impacts.

news.headline: FULTON COUNTY Waze offering Alpharetta , Johns Creek residents $2 carpools during summer
news.factual_summary: Alpharetta and Johns Creek residents could use Waze Carpool for $2 per ride through August 5 under a summer partnership. The app matched people traveling similar routes and allowed filters for coworkers, classmates, gender and route proximity. Councilman Chris Coughlin said the program aimed to reduce congestion and would serve as a test for other Georgia jurisdictions.

news.headline: Applied Information and HAAS Alert Announce Safety Cloud® Integration New collaborative partnership will deliver digital alerts to millions of connected vehicles for traffic signal preemption, collision prevention, and other vehicle and pedestrian safety applications.
news.factual_summary: Applied Information and HAAS Alert announced an integration linking connected roadside equipment and vehicles to Safety Cloud. Subscribed agencies would be able to deliver hazard alerts through Waze and supported vehicle infotainment systems. Planned capabilities include emergency-vehicle signal priority, active school-zone warnings and pedestrian-crossing alerts. The companies presented the partnership as a way to give drivers earlier warning and support responder and pedestrian safety.

news.headline: CITY TO JOIN IN ANONYMOUS SHARING OF TRAFFIC DATA
news.factual_summary: Pittsburgh introduced two proposed data-sharing agreements to City Council, one with Waze and another with the I-95 Corridor Coalition Traffic Flow Data Program. At no cost, the city would receive traffic, incident and travel-time information for construction planning and regional mobility analysis. Officials said the information was aggregated or anonymized and would not provide personal data about drivers or reporters.

news.headline: DIGITAL ENHANCEMENTS PROMOTE TRANSPARENCY, ACCOUNTABILITY
news.factual_summary: Fort Worth announced expanded public-data access through partnerships with the National Weather Service, Yelp and Waze, covering stormwater, restaurant inspections and traffic. City news and job openings were available through Amazon Echo, supplementing its OneAddress open-data program. The city also joined Bloomberg’s What Works Cities initiative for technical assistance.

news.headline: Braves announce Uber, Waze plan for Cobb stadium
news.factual_summary: The Atlanta Braves announced Uber and Waze components of their traffic plan for the new Cobb County stadium, including integrated parking guidance and a dedicated Uber pickup-and-drop-off lot. Officials described game-day intersection control, secured parking and possible shuttle services. The team expected congestion to improve after construction.

news.headline: How Google is endangering police officers
news.factual_summary: A CNN opinion writer argued that Waze’s police-location reporting endangered officers and could help offenders evade enforcement. The piece invoked the killing of two New York officers, alleged that the killer had used Waze beforehand, and criticized Google for declining discussions with the National Sheriffs’ Association.

news.headline: Partnering with tech companies lets cities serve citizens better
news.factual_summary: A municipal-technology article described Las Vegas’ planned Alexa city-services app, Coral Gables’ Uber promotional partnership and municipal Waze exchanges. Johns Creek had expanded its Waze sharing to business locations derived from licensing records. Las Vegas expected its app to be ready in 2017, while Coral Gables planned pickup zones and promotional codes. Officials and business representatives expected the partnerships to improve access to city services and local businesses.

news.headline: Waymo Has a New Job: Scanning for Potholes
news.factual_summary: Waymo announced a pilot using its autonomous vehicles to detect potholes and share locations through Waze for Cities and the Waze app. Users could verify detections. Initial coverage included the Bay Area, Los Angeles, Phoenix, Austin and Atlanta, where Waymo reported 500 identified potholes. The company planned to extend detection to other cities where it operates.

news.headline: AGENCIES PARTNERING FOR SAFE, IMPROVED THANKSGIVING TRAVEL
news.factual_summary: PennDOT and state police announced Thanksgiving traffic-management plans using historical and real-time 511PA data. Measures included extra patrols and tow coverage, targeted rerouting, adaptive signal management and coordination with emergency centers. PennDOT also described a portal prioritizing Waze user reports for staff.

news.headline: Uber partners with Boston on traffic data
news.factual_summary: Uber announced that it would share anonymized Boston trip data, including times, pickup and drop-off ZIP codes, distances and durations, with city planners. Officials expected an initial dataset within two weeks and quarterly updates, for uses such as traffic, parking and zoning analysis. Boston’s CIO described this as complementing its Waze partnership.

news.headline: MapQuest Opens Its Mapping Platform to AI Agents with a New Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server, Plus 1 Billion Free Transactions to Celebrate
news.factual_summary: MapQuest launched a hosted Model Context Protocol server giving compatible AI agents access to geocoding, routing and mapping tools through API-key authentication. It announced a shared promotional pool of one billion free transactions while supplies lasted, alongside existing free and paid plans. Described uses included address lookup, multi-stop directions and map generation inside agent applications.

news.headline: Louisville Metro Office of Civic Innovation Dreams Big to Win National Award
news.factual_summary: Louisville’s Office of Civic Innovation won the 2017 City on a Cloud Dream Big award for large cities. Its submission proposed using real-time data to adjust traffic management and support transit equity. The city described an internal Waze-data pilot, earlier cloud-based storage work and plans for a shared transportation-data warehouse, with some information to be published through its open-data portal.

news.headline: Technology Notebook: Improving Roadway Safety and Compliance
news.factual_summary: A roadway-technology roundup describes traffic analytics from Urban SDK, an open interface for Bentley’s Blyncsy platform, and compliance-management updates to J.J. Keller’s FleetMentor. It also reports that SH 130’s operator deployed Emergency Safety Solutions’ digital hazard alerts through connected vehicles and navigation apps. The updates are presented as tools for agencies and operators to monitor roads, manage compliance and warn drivers.

news.headline: Ford Partners with Apple to Integrate Maps in New EVs
news.factual_summary: A Ford stock report described plans to embed Apple Maps in its Universal Electric Vehicle platform beginning in 2027. Features would include traffic-aware directions, EV charging routes and battery preconditioning, while CarPlay and Android Auto remained supported. The report framed the partnership as part of Ford's software strategy and described later driver-assistance ambitions.

news.headline: Boston's betting on AI to take on traffic, records access and more
news.factual_summary: Boston implemented Google Project Green Light recommendations at intersections in Fenway, Mission Hill and Jamaica Plain after months of AI-assisted traffic analysis. Officials said they would continue assessing Maps-derived patterns alongside other sensor data. The article also describes a separate city experiment generating summaries and keywords for older City Council records, which officials said made the material easier to use.

news.headline: DAINES, KING INTRODUCE BILL TO REDUCE CROWDING ON PUBLIC LANDS AND SUPPORT PARTNERSHIPS WITH GATEWAY COMMUNITIES
news.factual_summary: Senators Steve Daines and Angus King introduced the Gateway Community and Recreation Enhancement Act to address crowded public lands and pressures on nearby communities. The proposed pilot would provide real-time visitor information and suggest less crowded recreation destinations, an idea King called “Waze for Parks.” The release described support from local-government, tourism and recreation groups seeking better visitor distribution and partnerships.

news.headline: Sanford sees weekend safety concerns as US -10 traffic crowds downtown
news.factual_summary: Michigan DOT closed US-10 beneath the M-30 bridge near Sanford after crews found cracks in newly installed beams. While the official detour used northern roads, navigation apps sent many drivers through downtown Sanford. Village officials raised concerns about heavy trucks and a weight-restricted bridge. Westbound lanes reopened Monday morning, with eastbound reopening planned that afternoon while replacement beams and project impacts were assessed.

news.headline: JOHNSON, CALABRESE INTRODUCE BILL TO REQUIRE NAVIGATIONAL APPS TO REROUTE DRIVERS AROUND EMERGENCY CONDITIONS
news.factual_summary: New Jersey Assemblymen Gordon Johnson and Clinton Calabrese introduced A-4222 in response to navigation-related traffic concerns in Leonia. The bill would let municipalities request review of emergency conditions and authorize the attorney general, after transport-department approval, to order app operators to reroute drivers. Noncompliance could bring fines up to $5,000 per day payable to the municipality. The proposal went to the Assembly Homeland Security and State Preparedness Committee.

news.headline: County sees troubling traffic trends
news.factual_summary: Dubuque County traffic counts showed substantial increases on roads near the Southwest Arterial after it opened. Engineer Anthony Bardgett proposed an axle restriction on Olde Davenport Road to deter heavy trucks using it as a shortcut and discussed asking Google Maps to change routing. Supervisors planned further consideration. A separate study found more truck traffic on gravel Christoph Road, raising concerns about maintenance and paving costs.

news.headline: Navigation Partnership With Alk Technologies
news.factual_summary: Webtech Wireless announced version 2.5 of its MDT 3100 in-cab terminal with ALK Technologies’ CoPilot Truck navigation, available for immediate delivery. Drivers could configure routes for vehicle dimensions and cargo restrictions. The release also added driver provisioning, automatic driver changes and cross-border hours-of-service support.

news.headline: Google Maps' new feature will show you where to park
news.factual_summary: Google announced destination guidance for Maps that highlights a destination, its entrance and nearby parking as drivers approach. The feature was due to roll out globally in the coming weeks, including supported in-car platforms. Maps also gained easier incident reporting, while Waze updates added camera types, traffic-event notices and planned locked-screen guidance.

news.headline: Mass. Bay Transportation Authority Bids Farewell to 2023 and Welcomes the New Year With Momentum: Infrastructure Investments, Workforce Growth, and With Improvements in Commuter Rail Ridership
news.factual_summary: The MBTA reported improvements at its 246 commuter-rail grade crossings, including reflective markings, bollards, road markers and brighter gate lights. It also partnered with Waze so commuter-rail crossings appear on the app’s maps and drivers receive advance alerts. The agency presented the physical and digital changes as measures to improve crossing visibility and driver awareness.

news.headline: Blumenthal wants mapping apps to include truck bans, low bridge warnings
news.factual_summary: Senator Richard Blumenthal urged Google and Apple to add commercial-vehicle restrictions to navigation apps after trucks entered Connecticut’s Merritt and Wilbur Cross parkways or struck bridges. He cited 581 truck-driver citations and 21 bridge strikes in the previous year and called for considering higher penalties and clearer signs. Police and preservation representatives described the hazards of truck drivers relying on passenger-car navigation.

news.factual_summary: ESCORT introduced its MAX 3 radar and laser detector at $399.99. The company described GPS-based filtering of repeated false alerts and a connection to the ESCORT Live app for shared reports about police, cameras, traffic and road hazards. It marketed the device as a complement to Waze, Google Maps and Apple Maps, combining detector signals with crowdsourced and database information.

news.factual_summary: Senator Richard Blumenthal urged Google, Apple and other mapping providers to add commercial-vehicle restrictions to navigation apps after trucks struck bridges or entered Connecticut’s Merritt and Wilbur Cross parkways. news.factual_summary: Google Maps added Android Auto route planning that suggests EV charging stops and estimates battery use, charging time and arrival charge. news.headline: L.A. Lawmakers Looking To Take Legal Action Against Google For Not Solving Long-Running City Traffic Problems
news.factual_summary: A Techdirt commentary criticized Los Angeles lawmakers’ consideration of legal action against Waze over neighborhood congestion. It discussed David Ryu’s request for legal review and complaints about routing onto steep Baxter Street. Google said maps would reflect road closures and turn restrictions imposed by the city. The writer argued that access and street-design decisions were city responsibilities and questioned efforts to make Google solve broader congestion problems.

news.headline: Navteq racing to provide more than GPS
news.factual_summary: NAVTEQ was broadening digital maps to include businesses and other points of interest alongside streets and turn restrictions. The report describes mapping teams gathering road data, the company’s growth in vehicle and online navigation, and competition from Tele Atlas, Google and user-generated maps. Chief executive Judson Green had pursued traffic-information and destination-mapping acquisitions to diversify the Chicago company.

news.headline: There is growing concern over where navigation apps sometimes tell you to go.
news.factual_summary: CBS reported residents’ complaints that navigation-app shortcuts brought heavy traffic and crashes to steep Baxter Street in Los Angeles. Neighbors described spinouts, stalled vehicles and property damage. City officials discussed one-way operation or turn restrictions, while Waze said a public road should be usable and encouraged reports of hazardous conditions. The segment also described Leonia’s rush-hour street restrictions as another community response.

news.headline: Don’t be the next carrier in the headlines for a bridge collapse — Here’s how to minimize risks of GPS routing
news.factual_summary: After truck drivers blamed GPS directions for bridge collapses and other routing incidents, trucking specialists urged fleets to use commercial navigation and enter accurate vehicle and load details. Manufacturers described truck restrictions, geofencing alerts and map updates. The article examined a Missouri bridge collapse and found differences among vendors’ restriction data, with TomTom saying it had requested missing weight-limit information for two cited bridges.

news.headline: MAYOR DE BLASIO SURPASSES OPEN STREETS TARGET, ANNOUNCES 13 MORE MILES OF STREETS TO BE OPENED BY ME
news.factual_summary: New York City announced 13 additional miles of Open Streets for May 23, bringing the program’s total to 43 miles. Streets would serve pedestrians and cyclists, with through traffic prohibited and limited local vehicle access at 5 mph. Google Maps already showed the previous 30 miles, with new locations to follow. The city also began installing nine miles of temporary cycling space.

news.headline: After Kids' Deaths, Chinatown Pedestrian Safety Plan Outlined
news.factual_summary: After an unattended van struck preschoolers on a Chinatown sidewalk, killing Hayley Ng and Diego Martinez, state Senator Daniel Squadron and Manhattan Borough President Scott Stringer called for a nine-point pedestrian-safety plan. Proposed actions included stronger enforcement, truck-route controls, delivery and parking management, traffic calming, wider sidewalks and community-led planning. The article also reports families’ accounts and residents’ criticism of existing traffic conditions.

news.headline: Drive Less Distracted With Assistant Integration In Waze
news.factual_summary: Google started rolling out Assistant voice controls in Waze for U.S. Android users in English. Drivers could request toll-free routes, report traffic using their current location and control messages or media while navigating. The article placed the update alongside other exchanges of features between Waze and Google Maps, including incident reporting and police alerts.

news.headline: A day in the life of a chief sustainability officer: Q&A with Google ’s Kate Brandt
news.factual_summary: Google chief sustainability officer Kate Brandt described working across product, customer and operations teams rather than following a fixed daily routine. Her examples include reviewing fuel-efficient routing with Google Maps, helping cloud customers use Earth Engine, and discussing clean-energy procurement and building materials. She connected this work with Google’s goals of net zero emissions and continuous local carbon-free energy by 2030.

news.headline: Top 10 Best Gas Finder Android Apps - 2022
news.factual_summary: A gas-finder app guide described Waze, AAA Mobile and MapQuest as tools combining navigation with fuel information. Waze showed nearby stations and prices alongside traffic alerts. AAA’s TripTik supported multi-stop planning with fuel locations and grades, while MapQuest compared prices along routes and offered route-avoidance settings. The selected entries presented these features as options for finding fuel during trips.

news.headline: Google Assistant takes the wheel in Waze to bring hands-free reports and directions
news.factual_summary: Google began integrating Assistant into Waze on Android, allowing voice reports of traffic and potholes and requests for alternate routes or toll avoidance. The interface kept turn-by-turn directions visible while processing commands. The article also described a separate Assistant driving mode planned for summer, with navigation, messaging, calling and media controls intended to replace the standalone Android Auto app.

news.headline: Why Google Maps' New Biking Directions Could Be Huge
news.factual_summary: Google announced bicycle directions in about 150 US cities, with routing that favored suitable trails and bike lanes and considered hills, busy roads and intersections. Suzanne Merkelson described cooperation with Rails-to-Trails Conservancy and suggested Google’s reach could introduce the feature to a wider audience. A mobile version was still planned.

news.headline: How to Save Money on Gas When Prices are High
news.factual_summary: A small-business guide proposed ways to manage rising fuel costs, including vehicle maintenance, gentler driving, lighter loads, combining errands and shared rides. It recommended comparing station prices with apps, reviewing rewards programs and using Google Maps or Waze to plan around congestion. The article also discussed vehicle efficiency and purchase choices, presenting these as options for reducing ongoing fuel spending.

news.factual_summary: GO Boulder and the City of Boulder launched GOBikeBoulder.net on June 21, 2007, inviting residents to test an online bicycle-routing service and submit feedback. The tool offered maps, turn-by-turn directions, on-street or off-street preferences, and estimates of climbing, calorie use and fuel savings. news.headline: Letters to the Editor
news.factual_summary: This Ridgefield letters collection contains four readers’ opinions. PA Torzilli criticized presidential misinformation; Joe Savino opposed Connecticut toll proposals and warned that Waze-assisted toll avoidance could increase neighborhood traffic. Lloyd Fremed urged Founders Hall to stop using polystyrene cups, citing health and environmental concerns. news.headline: Get Fit on the Fly
news.factual_summary: A magazine feature encouraged women to bicycle for transport, fitness and recreation, discussing confidence, route planning, clothing, equipment and comfort. Instructors recommended Google Maps’ bicycle mode as a way to identify routes and bike lanes.

news.factual_summary: Google announced plans to make its fuel-efficient routing technology available to third-party developers through Google Maps Platform in preview later in 2022. Delivery and ridesharing companies would be able to embed efficient routes in their apps, select engine types, and estimate fuel consumption and savings across trips or fleets. Google estimated earlier consumer use in the United States and Canada had avoided 500,000 metric tons of carbon emissions.

news.headline: More ways to drive sustainably and save money with Google Maps
news.factual_summary: Google began rolling out fuel-efficient routing in nearly 40 European countries and announced upcoming engine-type selections for drivers in Europe, the United States and Canada. Routes would account for petrol, diesel, hybrid or electric vehicles using models informed by government research and driving data. Google estimated that earlier U.S. and Canadian use had avoided over 500,000 metric tons of carbon emissions.

news.factual_summary: Google was expanding eco-friendly routing to nearly 40 European countries and preparing engine-specific efficiency estimates for users in Europe, the United States and Canada. news.headline: Valerie Bertinelli, On Finding Peace And Positivity Through Some Very Challenging Years
news.factual_summary: In a Today discussion of high gasoline prices, correspondent Sam Brock outlined fuel rewards, warehouse-club discounts and Google Maps’ fuel-efficient route option. He explained that route choices could trade additional time for less fuel use by accounting for hills and traffic. Presenters also discussed carpooling, cycling and the financial strain of fuel costs.

news.factual_summary: At Google Cloud Next ’22, Thomas Kurian announced that Cloud Carbon Footprint was generally available without charge in the cloud console to help customers examine emissions. He also highlighted Earth Engine’s availability for environmental analysis and announced plans to bring fuel-efficient Google Maps routing to developers and transportation companies, allowing delivery and ridesharing apps to incorporate those routes.

news.headline: Google Maps to offer energy-efficient routes tailored to electric vehicles, hybrids, more
news.factual_summary: Google Maps was preparing to expand fuel-efficient routing with options tailored to electric vehicles, hybrids and other vehicle types, according to a July 2022 report by 9to5Google.

news.headline: 5 Google Maps tips for less stress this holiday season
news.factual_summary: Google offered holiday travel tips using Maps: find stops along a route, share an estimated arrival time, compare nearby fuel prices, and choose fuel- or energy-efficient routes. It also highlighted indoor directories for malls, airports and transit stations, plus current and typical busyness information to help users plan visits and avoid crowds.

news.headline: Google Assistant Comes To Waze In Android To Help Keep Your Hands On The Wheel
news.factual_summary: Google announced Assistant integration in Waze for Android users in the United States, supporting voice-controlled calls, messages, media playback and traffic reports. The company said the feature would help drivers keep their hands on the wheel. The article also cited AAA Foundation and Texas transportation research describing distraction and slower reactions associated with voice commands or voice-to-text use.

news.headline: What's New With the Maps App in iOS 16: Multi-Stop Routing, Transit Card Support and More
news.factual_summary: Apple Maps in iOS 16 adds routes with up to 15 stops, Siri commands to insert stops, and the ability to plan a journey on a Mac and send it to an iPhone. Users arrange the stop order themselves. The update also integrates Wallet transit-card balances and refills, displays transit fares in selected cities, streamlines travel-mode controls, and expands Apple’s more detailed map design to additional countries.

news.headline: The Google Assistant is now available in Waze
news.factual_summary: Google announced the start of Google Assistant’s rollout in Waze for English-speaking Android users in the United States. Drivers could use voice commands to report traffic and potholes, check alternate routes and avoid tolls while navigating. Assistant also supported music, podcasts, messaging and calls within the navigation screen. Google presented the integration as a way to reduce distractions.

news.headline: Overlooked Google Maps features every road tripper should be using
news.factual_summary: A road-trip guide described using Google Maps to compare routes, review hotels and attractions, bookmark destinations and identify fuel or charging stops. The writer recommended offline maps, contingency stops, route sharing and desktop planning before sending directions to a phone. It also advised carrying paper maps and emergency supplies in case a phone or connection became unavailable.

news.headline: Google Maps for iOS Gains More Detail, Toll Estimates, and Standalone Apple Watch Support
news.factual_summary: Google announced more detailed iOS and CarPlay navigation maps, toll estimates and Apple Watch directions that would no longer require starting navigation on an iPhone. Other planned updates included a pinned-trip widget and integrations with Spotlight, Siri and Shortcuts. Availability varied by feature and region, with toll estimates planned first for about 2,000 roads in four countries.

news.headline: Multipronged anti-speeding effort succeeds in slowing traffic A combination of enforcement, engineering and public outreach successfully reduced speeding in a pilot project in rural Maryland.
news.factual_summary: A Maryland pilot on MD 367 combined wider lane markings, speed-feedback signs, public outreach and targeted police enforcement, including Waze advertising. IIHS researchers reported a 9% reduction in average speeds during the campaign and substantially lower odds of speeding. After enforcement, publicity and temporary engineering measures ended, effects weakened; average speeds remained 2% lower, while the most extreme speeding increased relative to baseline.

news.headline: App makers should take responsibility for the effects of their creations
news.factual_summary: A commentary argued that app developers should take responsibility for unintended effects, using reported Waze-directed neighborhood traffic as its main example. It described residents’ unsuccessful false reports and government responses such as turn restrictions and barriers, then advocated voluntary attention to consequences before stronger regulation.

news.headline: THE DELAWARE OFFICE OF HIGHWAY SAFETY ANNOUNCES "SAFE SUMMER ROADS 23" CAMPAIGN
news.factual_summary: Delaware’s Office of Highway Safety launched Safe Summer Roads for May 25 through September 4, combining education with high-visibility police enforcement. Separate patrol periods targeted impaired driving, speeding, seat-belt use and distraction. Outreach included DART Wi-Fi advertisements, community events and Waze messages shown while drivers were stopped reminding them to watch for pedestrians. Officials encouraged sober travel, visible walking attire and reduced phone distraction.

news.headline: Tweaking traffic in tech-savvy times
news.factual_summary: Traffic engineers described modifying streets so navigation apps would favor major roads over residential shortcuts. In Clyde Hill, Washington, speed enforcement, turn restrictions, roundabouts and ramp-meter adjustments increased cut-through journey times; engineer Eric Shimizu said drivers shifted toward Bellevue Way. Portland used bicycle-greenway diverters and planned lower residential speed limits. Officials also discussed cooperation with app developers and problems when maps lagged behind new restrictions.

news.headline: Why Mapping Apps Keep Traffic Engineers Up at Night
news.factual_summary: A JD Supra commentary explained tensions between apps optimizing individual journeys and engineers managing street safety and traffic distribution. It described turn restrictions, lower speeds and barriers intended to make residential shortcuts less attractive, while noting that traffic could shift elsewhere and drivers might follow outdated directions. The writer advocated incorporating broader public concerns into routing and described app data as a resource for planners.

news.headline: Roadway improvements, traffic safety research recognized in latest National Roadway Safety Awards
news.factual_summary: The report reviewed seven National Roadway Safety Award projects, including street redesign, work-zone warnings, pavement markings, speed-feedback signs and video analytics. Broward’s Wilton Drive changes were associated with reported reductions in crashes and improved travel times. Florida DOT’s pilot combined radar and warning signs, with Waze-linked information among tested tools. Other recipients used planning and design-analysis methods to identify safety improvements.

news.headline: City seeks solution for North Peak traffic
news.factual_summary: West Lake Hills City Council approved a North Peak Road traffic-calming plan and authorized a builder if costs stayed below $20,000. Measures included two speed cushions, striping and a possible stop-sign relocation. A council member attributed increased cut-through traffic partly to navigation apps.

news.headline: Open Forum: Bring back sanity to San Francisco s traffic-congested streets
news.factual_summary: Josh Wilson urged San Francisco residents and officials to address dangerous driving and neighborhood cut-through traffic, including routes suggested by Google Maps. He called for traffic-calming petitions, reporting hazardous intersections, consideration of traffic cameras and changes in driver behavior. The commentary discussed delayed safety improvements, Mayor London Breed’s push for faster action and WalkSF’s planned Walk to Work Day.

news.headline: Not so uplyfting
news.factual_summary: Divya Nekkanti described choosing a Berkeley bus over a surge-priced Lyft ride and using Apple Maps to follow the trip. She argued that ride-hailing convenience diverted riders from public transit, contributed to congestion and exposed drivers to insecure work. The column criticized neighborhood rerouting by navigation apps and urged greater transit ridership and investment, citing bus-lane and access initiatives.

news.headline: Rollingwood talks traffic issues City Council looks for fixes for volume of cars cutting through
news.factual_summary: Rollingwood council members discussed rising cut-through traffic near Austin’s Zilker Park and voted to request collaboration with Austin officials. Staff suspected navigation apps were directing drivers through Paige Drive and Riley Road. Possible responses included a no-left-turn sign, a barrier and speed bumps. The council also considered sports-field use, athletic-club plans and additional funding to complete city easement and utility mapping.

news.headline: People finding their 'waze' to once-hidden streets
news.factual_summary: Residents near Interstate 405 in Los Angeles complained that Waze-directed shortcuts had brought heavy traffic onto narrow neighborhood streets. Some discussed submitting false incident reports to deter drivers. Waze said subsequent users’ location data would negate coordinated false reports, while city officials described possible traffic-calming measures requiring study.

news.headline: Connected Vehicle Technology and Artificial Intelligence Transforming the Approach to Traffic Management in Central Texas The Central Texas Regional Mobility Authority has deployed Waycare to improve traffic incident management on its roads.
news.factual_summary: The Central Texas Regional Mobility Authority deployed Waycare to combine connected-vehicle and roadway-sensor data for traffic-incident management. The system alerted traffic-center staff to possible crashes and hazards for verification before notifying responders and drivers through Waze and Twitter. Partners were expanding coverage across the authority’s toll roads and developing direct alerts to connected vehicles, with wider regional deployment under discussion.

news.headline: PA TURNPIKE CAUTIONS DRIVERS TO EXPECT HEAVY TRAFFIC DURING US OPEN
news.factual_summary: Pennsylvania Turnpike officials warned of heavier traffic near Oakmont during the June 13–19 U.S. Open and announced shuttle service, additional staff and troopers, and towing restrictions near the event. They encouraged travelers to consult TRIP Talk, Waze and other information services.

news.headline: Smart Commute Market 2019-2023 Segmentation by Product Types, Growth Potential, Strategic Assessment, Technological Advancement, Comprehensive Analysis, Developments Status
news.factual_summary: Market Research Future promoted a report forecasting the global smart-commute market would reach $104.22 billion by 2023, with annual growth of 25.62% from 2018. Commissioner Russell McMurry said the arrangement would extend real-time awareness to arterial roads as well as highways.

news.headline: Protecting bus lanes
