news.headline: How Atlanta streamlines traffic flows
news.factual_summary: Atlanta worked with Esri and Waze after the I-85 bridge collapse to map live traffic reports and support transportation management. Esri’s GeoEvent Server processed user reports into displays for commuters and city officials, while CommuteATL incorporated transit, bicycle and bike-share information. The article describes using crowdsourced data to identify incidents and backups, coordinate responses and provide travelers with multiple transport options.

news.headline: DELAWARE DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION PROVIDES REAL TIME CROWD SOURCE TRAFFIC MANAGEMENT THROUGH NEW DATA EXCHANGE PARTNERSHIP
news.factual_summary: Delaware’s transportation department announced a free two-way Waze partnership. DelDOT would provide construction, closure and road-condition reports, while receiving anonymous user incidents and slowdown information to supplement traffic monitoring. Secretary Jennifer Cohan described it as an extension of the department’s mobile traveler-information tools and urged people to use phones while not driving. Officials expected the exchange to support travel choices and planning.

news.headline: Trafficware Delivers Most Comprehensive Functionality of Any ATMS System on the Market Releases Version 2.3 of ATMS.now Advanced Traffic Management System
news.factual_summary: Trafficware released version 2.3 of ATMS.now, adding public-facing congestion, incident and parking information, Google Maps functionality and expanded connected-vehicle controller data. The company also described improved reporting, database access and VIMOC parking integration. Customers with maintenance subscriptions would receive base-application features through that program.

news.headline: GOOG: Periodicals
news.factual_summary: A short market-news item reported that Waze announced Connected Citizens, a government partnership program to exchange crowdsourced traffic information with ten initial partners. It named cities and agencies including Boston, Los Angeles, Rio de Janeiro, Florida, Utah and the New York Police Department.

news.headline: Connected Car News: Bosch, Qualcomm , Frontenac , Honk Technologies, CurbsideSOS, Murata , Utah DOT , Parsons , Teletrac Navman , Waymo & Waze
news.factual_summary: Waymo and Waze announced an April 9, 2026 pilot adding autonomous-vehicle pothole detections to Waze for Cities. Transportation agencies would receive the data and Waze drivers could verify hazards. The initial markets were the Bay Area, Los Angeles, Phoenix, Austin and Atlanta, with about 500 reported detections and future expansion planned into regions affected by freeze-thaw damage.

news.headline: Beaumont early rush hour traffic light, for now
news.factual_summary: A Beaumont morning bulletin reported generally clear in-city highway travel except southbound U.S. 69 congestion between Delaware Street and Harrison Avenue. Outside the city, I-10 slowed in both directions near Din Bayou and the Hamshire exit, with Waze reports of stopped vehicles and thunderstorms. Showers were forecast to reach Beaumont later that morning.

news.headline: Moderate Friday night traffic through Beaumont
news.factual_summary: A Friday evening Beaumont traffic bulletin described generally light highway congestion at the start of 2026, based on TxDOT maps and Waze reports. Traffic began building on southbound U.S. 69 near the city's north end and westbound I-10 downtown approaching northbound U.S. 69. The report noted stopped vehicles on I-10 and anticipated heavier commuting when work and school resumed.

news.headline: Week starts with usual morning traffic
news.factual_summary: A Monday morning Beaumont traffic report described southbound U.S. 69 delays between Delaware Street and Harrison Avenue, with speeds at or below 25 mph. Westbound I-10 slowed from College Street toward the U.S. 69 south exit, where Waze users reported about 10 mph. Eastbound and northbound traffic remained clearer; the bulletin also anticipated gusty weather later that morning.

news.headline: Study Results from University of California Provide New Insights into Information Technology (A Comparative Study of Freeway Travel Times from Four Data Sources)
news.factual_summary: University of California researchers compared Waze, HERE and INRIX travel-time estimates with Caltrans Bluetooth data on I-80 between Davis and Sacramento. The study found that HERE and INRIX more closely matched the benchmark, while all three vendors’ data deteriorated as congestion increased. Researchers reported systematic differences in Waze estimates associated with disturbances, segment-length discrepancies, segment length and traffic volume.

news.headline: Fixing Seattle 's Traffic Mess
news.factual_summary: Cliff Mass argued that Seattle could address congestion by reversing road diets, improving pavement, limiting bridge openings, strengthening rail and last-mile options, and restricting device use while driving. He used Google Maps traffic displays and personal observations to support criticisms of city choices.

news.headline: Tech that lets you knows about a crash ahead of time A Chicago-headquartered startup plays a role in road safety by curbing accidents between drivers and emergency vehicles
news.factual_summary: HAAS Alert expanded its Safety Cloud service for broadcasting emergency-vehicle and roadway-hazard warnings to drivers. The report describes the Chicago company’s Detroit office, partnerships with more than 50 Michigan communities and integrations with Waze and supported vehicle systems. Cofounder Cory Hohs recounted the company’s shift from detecting sirens to transmitting digital alerts, with agencies paying subscriptions. The company said digital warnings could help drivers respond sooner to emergency vehicles and hazards.

news.headline: Multipronged Anti-Speeding Effort Succeeds in Slowing Traffic
news.factual_summary: A Maryland pilot on MD 367 combined wider lane markings, speed-feedback signs, public outreach and targeted police enforcement, including Waze advertising. Researchers reported 9% lower average speeds during the campaign and lower odds of speeding. After the measures ended, effects weakened: average speeds remained 2% lower, while the odds of exceeding the limit by more than 10 mph were higher than before.

news.headline: Lane Change?
news.factual_summary: The National Park Service proposed replacing Rock Creek and Potomac Parkway’s rush-hour one-way operation with permanent two-way traffic. Officials cited higher speeds and a disproportionate share of crashes during reversible-lane hours, plus the work of manually changing traffic controls. Opponents predicted worse congestion and residential diversions, while the Park Service argued two-way access could draw opposite-direction traffic off city streets.

news.headline: SDOT Announces 3rd Avenue Improvements
news.factual_summary: Seattle transport agencies announced expanded Third Avenue car restrictions for September 2018 and stop improvements for March 2019. Plans included all-day left-turn bans, removal of parking on Prefontaine Place, ORCA readers and real-time arrival signs. Seattle Transit Blog welcomed the changes and argued for stronger enforcement and clearer bus-only treatment to keep general traffic from delaying transit.

news.headline: App brings CoPilot Live to iPhone
news.factual_summary: ALK announced an iPhone version of CoPilot Live Truck, described as immediately downloadable from Apple’s app store. The announcement says routing used vehicle dimensions, weight and load type to account for commercial-truck restrictions in North America. ALK said the app offered safer, more reliable and less expensive navigation.

news.headline: VDOT WILL LIFT LANE CLOSURES TO EASE THANKSGIVING TRAVEL THE NEW VERSION OF THE 511 TRAVELER APP OFFERS CURRENT TRAFFIC CONDITIONS AND PUSH NOTIFICATIONS
news.factual_summary: VDOT announced that most major-road lane closures would be suspended from November 22 to November 27 for Thanksgiving travel. It promoted a historical congestion map and an updated 511 app showing cameras, incidents and travel options, with a link into Waze for navigation. The advisory also listed holiday HOV schedules and warned that some permanent work zones would remain.

news.headline: TRUCK NOISE IN SOUTHWEST DETROIT ADDS TO PUBLIC HEALTH CONCERNS
news.factual_summary: University of Michigan researchers and Southwest Detroit residents measured noise at 21 homes to study truck-traffic impacts. They combined sound monitoring, vehicle counts, photographs and Google Maps information and reported higher noise near truck routes, including levels exceeding cited guidelines. Community partners hoped the findings would inform truck-route changes as the Gordie Howe International Bridge was built, while residents described sleep disruption and difficulty using outdoor space.

news.headline: Waze Adds Voice Commands, Motorcycle Mode, Carpool Lanes
news.factual_summary: Waze added hands-free OK Waze commands, motorcycle mode and support for carpool lanes. Users could request directions and trip information by voice, configure HOV eligibility or passes, and select motorcycles for tailored routing. The article listed initial English-speaking markets and HOV coverage in U.S. states and selected Canadian cities. Waze said routing would improve as more motorcycle users supplied data.

news.headline: Wheaton commissions intersection traffic study Traffic: Hoping to combat speeders
news.factual_summary: Wheaton hired an engineering consultant to study traffic calming at Harrison Avenue and Washington Street after crashes and earlier speed studies raised concerns. The approved contract allows up to $17,600 plus contingency for data review, recommendations and preliminary cost estimates. Officials cited speeding, impatient turning and sight-distance issues and hoped the findings could guide changes at other locations.

news.headline: Mount Prospect weighs options to slow traffic through Hatlen Heights
news.factual_summary: Mount Prospect trustees were to consider a $30,000 traffic-calming plan for Hatlen Heights, including mini traffic circles, speed-feedback signs, a four-way stop and pavement markings. The Transportation Safety Commission unanimously recommended the measures following a May trial. Village officials reported about 70% fewer drivers exceeding 35 mph during the trial; residents supported several measures but opposed proposed raised entrance islands.

news.headline: Philly gets $13M for traffic-calming projects
news.factual_summary: PennDOT announced $13 million in grants for six Philadelphia traffic-safety projects funded by automated speed-enforcement revenue. Work included $2 million for further Lincoln Drive traffic calming, speed humps near 100 additional schools, signal and intersection planning, and safety improvements on commercial and transit corridors. The article also noted upcoming activation of cameras in five school zones.

news.headline: Beaumont road upgrades focus on traffic safety, flow
news.factual_summary: Beaumont Public Works Director Molly Villarreal described road diets, turn lanes, bicycle facilities, lighting, accessible ramps and signal upgrades intended to improve street safety and traffic organization. She said the city was also pursuing adaptive signals, vehicle sensors and digital speed-feedback signs, supported by grant applications. Claimed reductions in delays and crashes were presented as the rationale for the work.

news.headline: Traffic light planned for dangerous road
news.factual_summary: New York DOT announced a $4.2 million Route 7 safety project in Niskayuna after a study recorded five fatal crashes in three years. Plans included narrower lanes, raised medians, a signal and pedestrian crossing at Hickory Road, relocation of a hospital entrance and turn restrictions. Construction was expected the following spring, with completion by the end of 2027 and June public open houses.

news.headline: How one Massachusetts city cut traffic deaths to zero Somerville, Massachusetts, improved its traffic safety by committing to the unglamorous, but effective, work of doubling down on proven road safety tools and community outreach.
news.factual_summary: Somerville reported three years without a traffic death and declining serious-injury crashes after years of speed management and street redesign. The article described lower limits, 139 speed humps since 2019, raised crossings and curb extensions, alongside resident advisory work and community walks. Officials and advocates credited sustained leadership, physical changes and public engagement for the city's safety progress.

news.headline: After a fatal hit-and-run, a Philly mom fights for traffic safety
news.factual_summary: Philadelphia mother Angela McDonald sought speed humps, street redesign and cameras near South 58th and Delancey streets after her son Mark Ringgold was killed in a hit-and-run. Family and advocates marked the anniversary with a neighborhood walk. A council office was pursuing safety treatments, while a nearby Slow Zone was underway. Police had recovered the vehicle but had made no arrest.

news.headline: Oak Harbor Council gives red light to traffic cameras
news.factual_summary: Oak Harbor council members expressed reluctance to pursue automated traffic cameras after a workshop on costs, staffing and potential school- and park-zone locations. Members favored additional speed data, traffic calming and police enforcement before committing. Police and engineering staff described existing data subscriptions, speed-feedback signs and crossing improvements that could guide further decisions.

news.headline: TEMPORARY TRAFFIC SIGNAL TO BEGIN OPERATION ON WINDMILL POINT ROAD IN LANCASTER
news.factual_summary: VDOT scheduled a temporary traffic signal and 25-mph work-zone limit on Windmill Point Road in Lancaster County beginning October 12. Alternating one-way traffic will continue during replacement of the Oyster Creek bridge, expected to finish in May 2027. A temporary single-lane bridge will carry traffic later in the fall. The $10.3 million project replaces the 1930 bridge with wider lanes and shoulders.

news.headline: MAYOR BRANDON JOHNSON, CDOT DELIVER NEW TRAFFIC SAFETY IMPROVEMENTS AROUND SCHOOLS ACROSS CHICAGO
news.factual_summary: Chicago officials announced completed school-zone traffic improvements, including speed humps, curb extensions, pedestrian islands, lower speed limits, and a protected bike lane serving six Englewood schools. The release also lists projects completed in Albany Park, West Garfield Park, West Lawn, and Edgewater. CDOT says designs draw on crash history, street conditions, school operations, and community feedback as part of broader citywide safety work.

news.headline: Toss out the road atlas and check out the Web
news.factual_summary: David Rampe’s 1996 article compares free web mapping and trip-planning services, including MapQuest, Yahoo, Microsoft, DeLorme and Excite. It describes printable directions, address maps and points of interest, while reporting inaccurate urban routes and limits on multipoint planning. MapQuest said better city routing required detailed information about one-way streets and turn restrictions and announced international city maps.

news.headline: Pharos Utilizes EtakMap Premium to Enhance its Pocket PC Navigator GPS Software
news.factual_summary: Etak announced that Pharos had licensed EtakMap Premium data for Pocket PC Navigator, software providing GPS maps and driving directions on Microsoft Pocket PCs. The October 2000 release describes nationwide street coverage, turn restrictions, voice prompts, off-route warnings and rerouting. It states that the navigator had been released on July 31 and could work with various GPS receivers.

news.headline: Take a left on the next sidewalk
news.factual_summary: Richard Folkers’s 1999 report examines errors in free online directions from MapQuest and MapBlast, including routes onto a footpath or a nonexistent road. It describes how mapping companies combined geographic, postal and local-government information with field checks. The article explains that shortest, fastest and simplest route settings could each produce unsuitable results and recommends verifying directions. Mapping-company representatives acknowledged data limitations and overstatements in marketing.

news.headline: deCarta Introduces Software Developer Kit for Fast-Growing Personal Navigation Market
news.factual_summary: San Jose software company deCarta announced a navigation software development kit for personal navigation devices and smartphones. It described customizable maps and interfaces, multipoint routing, toll-road and freeway avoidance, time-dependent turn restrictions, and voice and graphical guidance. The company proposed later connections to live traffic, weather and local-search services. General availability was scheduled for early 2007 on Windows CE and later that year on Linux.

news.headline: Friendly signage on way to Jersey borough that closed roads
news.factual_summary: Leonia planned to replace Do Not Enter signs with signs saying Residents and Leonia Destinations Only after businesses reported that visitors were being discouraged from shopping and dining. Mayor Judah Zeigler said the revised wording would clarify access during rush-hour restrictions on residential streets. The town faced a lawsuit and planned protest, while the mayor said officials would keep monitoring unintended effects.

news.headline: Illinois GPS Task Force Releases Report to General Assembly The Global Positioning System Technology and Designated Truck Route System Task Force results could provide a template for other jurisdictions
news.factual_summary: An Illinois task force submitted recommendations on truck GPS and designated routes to the governor and legislature. It identified fragmented state and local restriction data and proposed combining databases, simplifying local reporting, improving industry access and educating drivers about truck-specific devices. Supporters said the recommendations could reduce bridge strikes, repairs and congestion.

news.headline: Apple Country Transit Announces Partnership with Google Maps
news.factual_summary: Henderson County announced that Apple Country Public Transit route data had been integrated into Google Maps. Riders could plan trips by departure or arrival time, including through mobile apps and links from the transit website. County planning, addressing, IT and legal staff coordinated the project with Google. Officials cited free participation, multilingual information and screen-reader support among the service’s features.

news.headline: Google Maps makes transit tracking easier
news.factual_summary: Pullman Transit routes became available in Google Maps, allowing passengers to enter destinations and planned departure or arrival times and receive bus and walking connections. The article compared the integrated trip suggestions with existing route maps in the Washington State University app and Pullman Transit’s Where’s My Bus website. It explained how agencies supply stop, route, schedule and fare data through Google’s Transit Partner Program.

news.headline: Gwinnett
news.factual_summary: Peachtree Corners joined Waze’s Connected Citizens Program to exchange traffic information. The city would receive real-time reports from app users and traffic information for local roads, while supplying advance notice of construction, planned street closures and major events. The partnership aimed to help motorists plan routes around disruptions.

news.headline: ASU , City of Phoenix Announce Circular Economy Incubator Ventures
news.factual_summary: Arizona State University and Phoenix selected FLI Right, rePurpose, Scrappy & Scraps Pet Treats and Recyclops for a circular-economy incubator supporting waste-prevention and reuse businesses. Participants would receive workshops, technical assistance and mentoring. Recyclops used independent pickup-truck contractors and a routing app to offer recycling in underserved areas. Officials described opportunities for participating businesses to compete for city waste-diversion projects.

news.headline: Virginia Beach: City's Chief Information Officer Wins National Technology Leadership Award
news.factual_summary: Virginia Beach CIO Peter Wallace won a Local IT Leader of the Year award, and the city’s traffic-data partnership won a Local IT Innovation award in StateScoop’s 2020 LocalSmart Awards. The city described its Waze partnership as providing real-time government construction, crash and closure information to travelers. The release also outlined Wallace’s technology leadership and regional connectivity work.

news.headline: Waze Will Now Help You Find EV Charging Stations
news.factual_summary: Waze began rolling out electric-vehicle charging locations to U.S. users in partnership with Volkswagen. Drivers could view nearby stations, add one to a route and save it for later use. The partnership also offered a Volkswagen ID.4 vehicle avatar. The article described the feature as a new option for Waze users seeking charging information during trips.

news.headline: FREE RTD PUBLIC TRANSIT FOR ALL IN AUG.
news.factual_summary: Boulder County announced that all RTD services, including airport buses, would be free from August 1 through 31 under Colorado’s Zero Fare for Better Air initiative. Supported by Senate Bill 22-180, the program aims to encourage transit use during the high-ozone season. County officials promoted route planning through Transit App, Google Maps and RTD’s trip planner, alongside existing programs that support bus access, bicycling and alternatives to driving.

news.headline: MASSDOT RELEASES BICYCLIST GUIDE AHEAD OF ORANGE LINE CLOSURE BEGINNING AUG. 19
news.factual_summary: MassDOT, the MBTA and local partners compiled a bicyclist guide ahead of the Orange Line’s 30-day shutdown beginning August 19 and a Green Line closure beginning August 22. The guide provides recommended routes, safety tips and resources. Google Maps links and planned route signs direct cyclists away from streets heavily used by replacement buses, including Sullivan Square, Rutherford Avenue, Charles River Dam Road and Martha Road.

news.headline: Here's a map of 3M Half Marathon route road closures in Austin on Sunday
news.factual_summary: Austin’s 3M Half Marathon was set to bring rolling road closures from 6 a.m. to noon Sunday, running from Stonelake Boulevard and Capital of Texas Highway to San Jacinto Boulevard near the Capitol. A San Jacinto segment would close Saturday. Organizers recommended major highways as alternatives and Google Maps or Waze for traffic information, noting that race closures had been submitted to both services in advance.

news.headline: 13:33 EST Google , Mercedes-Benz announce long-term strategic partnership for navigation
news.factual_summary: Mercedes-Benz and Google announced a long-term partnership to build branded in-car navigation using Google Maps Platform in the upcoming Mercedes-Benz Operating System. Planned capabilities include place information, live and predictive traffic, and automatic rerouting. The companies also planned YouTube integration, while Mercedes-Benz would use map data for assisted-driving functions such as adjusting speed before intersections, curves and roundabouts.

news.headline: Christmas travel plans in danger? Live updates on flight delays, cancellations and traffic
news.factual_summary: A holiday travel update warned that rain and snow could disrupt Christmas and New Year’s journeys across the central United States. It cited INRIX forecasts for heavy road traffic on December 23 and several days after Christmas, and advised checking navigation apps and highway-agency closure information. At the update’s publication, it reported no major flight-cancellation or delay disruption.

news.headline: Authorities offer spring break travel tips to cut stress, increase safety
news.factual_summary: Texas authorities increased traffic enforcement for spring break through March 17, targeting speeding, impaired driving and seat-belt violations. Officials urged sober travel, passenger handling of navigation apps and moving over for roadside responders. San Antonio airport expected about 203,000 travelers March 7–16 and advised arriving early, while TSA expanded screening capacity for the busy period.

news.headline: 'No driver, no hands, no clue': San Bruno police officers were met with a first after pulling over a Waymo
news.factual_summary: San Bruno police stopped an empty Waymo vehicle after an apparent illegal U-turn and contacted the company instead of issuing a driver citation. Waymo said it was investigating. The report describes posted turn restrictions and earlier autonomous-vehicle incidents, and notes California legislation allowing notices of autonomous-vehicle noncompliance beginning July 2026.

news.headline: Google just made following the Winter Olympics way easier
news.factual_summary: Google described tools for following the February 6–22, 2026 Winter Olympics in northern Italy. Search would provide schedules, results and medal counts, while YouTube would carry broadcaster highlights and creator coverage. For attendees, Google Maps and Waze would incorporate local road closures and transit schedules; Gemini-assisted Maps navigation and Waze community information were presented as additional travel tools.

news.headline: Dirt bikers create ‘havoc’ on Bay Bridge; massive traffic backup clears
news.factual_summary: Oakland police and CHP stopped a large group of dirt-bike and ATV riders near the Bay Bridge's eastern end on Sunday, briefly closing all eastbound lanes and causing a long backup. CHP reported 50 to 60 impounded vehicles and two Oakland police arrests. Traffic largely cleared by 8 p.m.; Google Maps had suggested an alternate bridge route during the disruption.

news.headline: Slow down, move over A shared responsibility to save Utahns this Memorial Day
news.factual_summary: AAA Utah urged Memorial Day travelers to slow down and move over for stopped vehicles, citing risks to roadside workers and forecasts of heavy holiday traffic. The organization described flashing truck signs and HAAS Alert integration delivering warnings through navigation apps and vehicle systems. It also advised avoiding distractions and impairment, looking ahead and changing lanes when safe.

news.headline: 13:26 EDT Google Maps debuts new 'immersive view' for cities in Google Maps
news.factual_summary: Google announced an immersive Maps view combining Street View and aerial imagery into a digital model of places. The company said users would be able to preview neighborhoods, landmarks, restaurants and venues before visiting. Its I/O announcement also highlighted fuel-efficient routing and bringing Live View capabilities to third-party apps.

news.headline: 12 Shopping Tricks to Keep You Under Budget
news.factual_summary: A shopping-budget guide recommended comparing gasoline prices through Google Maps, Waze or AAA rather than stopping at the first station. Expert Trae Bodge also highlighted Google Maps’ fuel-efficient route indicator and warehouse-club fuel discounts. The selected advice linked trip planning and comparison shopping to managing higher fuel costs.

news.headline: 12 Shopping Tricks to Keep You Under Budget
news.factual_summary: Shopping expert Trae Bodge recommends comparing nearby fuel prices through Google Maps, Waze or AAA rather than stopping at the first station. She also points to Maps’ fuel-efficient route option as a way to reduce fuel spending. Another tip suggests buying fuel at warehouse clubs when shoppers already hold memberships, combining a grocery visit with access to member fuel prices.

news.headline: CarPlay and Google Maps settings I was glad I changed before my road trip
news.factual_summary: A writer preparing for a cross-country move described adjusting Google Maps route preferences, downloading offline areas and entering vehicle details before a road trip. For CarPlay, the writer recommended removing unused apps, prioritizing essential icons and choosing readable appearance settings. The article also discussed widgets for weather and calendar information and the tradeoff between toll avoidance and longer travel.

news.headline: BULKY WASTE & MATTRESS RECYCLING EVENT
news.factual_summary: Lake Oswego and Republic Services scheduled a free resident-only bulky-waste drop-off event for October 4, 2025, from 9 a.m. to noon at 4101 Kruse Way. Accepted items include furniture, selected appliances, scrap metal, clean untreated wood and mattresses, with mattress recycling provided through the Mattress Recycling Council. The notice lists excluded materials and preparation requirements for equipment.

news.headline: Making infrastructure tech a reality in your portfolio
news.factual_summary: An infrastructure-investment analysis argued that smart-road technology could create opportunities through toll-road upgrades, connected systems and traffic management. It cited Boston analysts using Waze congestion data to adjust Seaport District signals and reporting an 18% reduction at key intersections. Another example described adaptive signals in New Jersey’s Meadowlands and agency estimates of reduced delays and emissions.

news.headline: Texas 130 in Pflugerville becomes Texas ’ first AI-powered ‘smart corridor’
news.factual_summary: TxDOT and Cavnue unveiled a $6 million, four-mile smart-corridor pilot on Texas 130 in Pflugerville, installing 66 AI-enabled cameras to detect hazards and alert traffic-management staff. Officials described faster incident response as an intended benefit. Direct alerts to navigation apps were being tested, and TxDOT planned to evaluate performance before possible wider deployment, including during I-35 reconstruction.

news.headline: Digital emergency alerts could help reroute robotaxis, company says
news.factual_summary: HAAS Alert proposed integrating its Safety Cloud emergency-vehicle warnings with autonomous-driving platforms so robotaxis could avoid active response scenes. Company executive Brock Aun said discussions involved major AV firms, while existing alerts already reached human drivers through vehicle screens, Waze and Apple Maps. He described potential real-time rerouting and longer-term risk analysis; AV pilots or deployments remained unannounced.

news.headline: Insurance Institute for Highway Safety: Multipronged Anti-Speeding Effort Succeeds in Slowing Traffic
news.factual_summary: A Maryland pilot on MD 367 combined wider lane markings, speed-feedback signs, public outreach and targeted police enforcement, including Waze advertising. IIHS researchers reported a 9% reduction in average speeds during the campaign and substantially lower odds of speeding. After enforcement, publicity and temporary engineering measures ended, effects weakened; average speeds remained 2% lower, while the most extreme speeding increased relative to baseline.

news.headline: Minor congestion on Beaumont highways
news.factual_summary: A Beaumont morning traffic bulletin described generally easy highway travel, apart from recurring southbound U.S. 69 congestion between Delaware Street and Harrison Avenue. Waze users reported reduced speeds through the narrowed section. I-10 in both directions showed no unusual backups, although construction zones continued to require slower, cautious travel.

news.headline: No Headline In Original
news.factual_summary: A City News Service roundup reported that Caltrans would share statewide closures and road-condition information directly with Waze. A Waze representative said the feed would fill gaps in data already supplied through Los Angeles city and Metro partnerships.

news.headline: THIS MAP SHOWS WHERE PEOPLE CAN ACCESS FOOD IN BUFFALO DURING COVID-19
news.factual_summary: University at Buffalo researchers created a Google Maps-based directory of grocery stores, food pantries, soup kitchens and school meal-pickup sites during COVID-19. Users could search neighborhoods, filter for free food and view contact information. The project supported Seeding Resilience, a community coalition coordinating food production and distribution. Residents supplied updates, while bicycle couriers and volunteer drivers helped transport food.

news.headline: MIDDLE SCHOOL STUDENTS LEARN THE IMPORTANCE OF HEAT RESILIENCE IN COMMUNITIES
news.factual_summary: Virginia Tech researchers worked with Roanoke middle-school students on a two-week heat-resilience program. Students used Google Maps and Street View to predict temperatures, then compared estimates with handheld sensors, infrared cameras and drone imagery. They discussed neighborhood cooling proposals and how heat affected daily life. Researchers planned to study how environmental data could support community participation in resilience decisions.

news.headline: BURLINGTON COUNTY LAUNCHES NEW ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT WEB SITE FOR RIVER ROUTE CORRIDOR COMMUNITIES
news.factual_summary: Burlington County announced a River Route website promoting redevelopment opportunities along New Jersey’s Route 130 corridor. The release describes links to available-property records, participating municipalities and Google Maps, developed through the county’s technology staff and River Route Advisory Committee. Officials presented the website as a marketing tool for 12 corridor towns and cited earlier investment and awards for the wider initiative.

news.headline: Travelers disagree on the usefulness of online mapping services such as Mapquest
news.factual_summary: Pittsburgh mapmaker Bob Firth criticized MapQuest, Google and Yahoo directions that appeared to require an illegal left turn downtown, and argued that step-by-step instructions could distract travelers from road signs and geographic context. Other users described both useful directions and routing errors. MapQuest representatives defended its accuracy and described how complaints reached mapping-data suppliers; Yahoo recommended retaining a paper map.

news.headline: Travelers disagree on the usefulness of Mapquest, other online mapping services.

news.headline: ROADGUY Car running unattended? You may soon be walking
news.factual_summary: A Minneapolis Roadguy column discussed the risk of leaving cars running unattended and reported a driver’s complaint after being ticketed for an illegal left turn onto Central Avenue. The driver said MapQuest had directed the turn, although signs and barricades prohibited it after traffic changes following the Interstate 35W bridge collapse. A MapQuest spokeswoman said software could miss temporary closures and drivers should heed restrictions.

news.headline: BIG BLUE MOVE-IN BEGINS AUG. 16; ANTICIPATE PARKING, TRAVEL IMPACTS
news.factual_summary: The University of Kentucky announced traffic and parking restrictions for more than 8,000 students moving into residence halls August 16–19. Plans included no-parking areas, temporary one-way streets, modified campus bus routes and designated parking. Students received residence-specific QR codes linking to Waze directions. Separate hospital construction also limited turns near University Drive and Cooper Drive.

news.headline: PORTION OF PIONEERS BOULEVARD TO CLOSE FEBRUARY 8 FOR RAILROAD REPAIRS
news.factual_summary: Lincoln scheduled closure of Pioneers Boulevard between Nebraska Highway 2 and U.S. 77 on February 8 from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. BNSF planned to raise and repair the crossing tracks east of South Ninth Street. Local access would remain available, with through traffic directed via West Van Dorn Street. City closure information and Waze were listed for updates.

news.headline: Q4 2020 Shake Shack Inc Earnings Call - Final
news.factual_summary: Shake Shack management said its marketing plans would emphasize new menu offerings and improvements to digital and in-restaurant experiences. The company described investment in digital products and data capabilities to support more personalized communications. It cited recent marketing partnerships with Waze and YouTube, alongside social-media activity and planned chef collaborations.

news.headline: Top 10 Best Android Navigation Apps - 2019
news.factual_summary: Android Headlines selected ten Android navigation apps and described their features, without ranking them. The list included Google Maps, HERE WeGo, Waze, Polaris, TomTom, MAPS.ME, Sygic, MapFactor, Karta and OsmAnd. It compared offline maps, traffic information, transit directions, outdoor navigation and route guidance. Waze’s entry highlighted live driver reports, route adjustments, gas-price information and Android Auto support.

news.headline: The new Apple Maps website is missing a lot vs. Google Maps
news.factual_summary: Apple launched a browser-based Maps beta with driving and walking directions, business listings and curated guides. A technology analysis compares it with Google Maps and Apple’s native app, arguing that broader routing, account syncing and personal lists would make it more competitive. It highlights Google’s direct gas-price comparisons and business-busyness information, while noting Apple planned to add Look Around imagery later.

news.headline: VDOT LIFTS LANE CLOSURES FOR CHRISTMAS AND NEW YEAR'S TRAVEL
news.factual_summary: VDOT announced plans to suspend most major-road work zones for Christmas and New Year travel, while listing continuing restrictions and holiday HOV schedules. It promoted 511Virginia and its new Waze data exchange for real-time conditions, and described temporary facilities at rebuilt rest areas.

news.headline: You re Already Using AI : Here s Where It s At In Everyday Life, From Facial Recognition To Navigation Apps
news.factual_summary: An overview of everyday artificial intelligence describes facial recognition, streaming recommendations, navigation and voice assistants. For Google Maps, it explains how text recognition extracts information from Street View imagery and how historical and live traffic data support travel-time predictions. The article also discusses adoption surveys and privacy concerns, including companies’ use of human reviewers to improve voice-assistant transcription.

news.headline: LOUDOUN COUNTY TRANSIT TO ADJUST STERLING BUS ROUTE 323 BEGINNING OCTOBER 1
news.factual_summary: Loudoun County Transit scheduled Route 323 changes in Sterling for October 1, 2025, adding Glenn Drive stops serving Women Giving Back and Loudoun Hunger Relief’s new pantry. The route would continue serving the library, community center and Innovation Center Metro with a revised schedule. Riders were directed to county updates, Google Maps and Transit for stop and service details.

news.headline: Connected Car News Tips: Renesas, Nuro, Green Hills, Forseight, Iteris, BlackBerry, TTTech, BMW, ON Semi, NXP, Cognata Eaton
news.factual_summary: A connected-car news roundup reported that Google Maps on Android was displaying roadwork and crash incident reports and allowing users to add incidents. The item presented the change as a new traffic-information feature.

news.headline: Where to bike safely on Pittsburgh side streets
news.factual_summary: A Pittsburgh cycling guide described Neighborways, designated side-street routes using signs and traffic calming to connect bicycle lanes and trails. Examples included routes through the South Side, Bloomfield-Friendship, Lawrenceville, Highland Park, Point Breeze and Shadyside. Eligible streets have low traffic volumes and 25 mph limits. The article directed riders to Bike Pittsburgh's map for precise routes.

news.headline: U.S. HIGHWAY 95 LANE CLOSURES, UPGRADES WEDNESDAY NIGHT IN CLARK COUNTY
news.factual_summary: Nevada’s transportation department planned to reduce U.S. 95 to one lane in each direction between mile markers 99 and 100 in Clark County from 9 p.m. June 3 to 5 a.m. June 4. MC4 would install traffic-count loop detectors near Snow Mountain Road. NDOT directed drivers to use caution and consult Waze or state services for restrictions.

news.headline: HENDERSON "SPAGHETTI BOWL" EVENING RAMP CLOSURE, UPGRADE JUNE 4
news.factual_summary: Nevada’s transportation department scheduled closure of the eastbound 215 Beltway ramp to northbound U.S. 95 in Henderson from 9 p.m. June 4 to 5 a.m. June 5. Contractor MC4 would install loop detectors for traffic counts. The advisory directed motorists to alternate routes and said NDOT shared planned restrictions through Waze.

news.headline: I-15 SOUTHBOUND OFFRAMP TO SAHARA AVE. CLOSED OVERNIGHT JUNE 14 IN LAS VEGAS
news.factual_summary: Nevada’s transportation department scheduled closure of the southbound Interstate 15 exit to Sahara Avenue and Highland Drive/Western Avenue in Las Vegas from 9 p.m. June 15 to 5 a.m. June 16. MC4 would install traffic-count loop detectors. NDOT advised alternate routes and identified Waze and state traffic services as update sources.

news.headline: GOP pushes back on two bills on California governor's desk
news.factual_summary: California AB 2015 and AB 2168 awaited Governor Gavin Newsom's signature after legislative passage. The first would require study of navigation-app impacts in a selected area; the second would broaden uses of transportation funding. Republicans criticized diversion from road repair, while CalBike supported more effective use of oversubscribed active-transportation funds.

news.headline: University of Michigan : Truck Noise in Southwest Detroit Adds to Public Health Concerns
news.factual_summary: University of Michigan researchers and Southwest Detroit residents measured noise at 21 homes to study truck-traffic impacts. They combined sound monitoring, vehicle counts, photographs and Google Maps information and reported higher noise near truck routes, including levels exceeding cited guidelines. Community partners hoped the findings would inform truck-route changes as the Gordie Howe International Bridge was built, while residents described sleep disruption and difficulty using outdoor space.
